items.title: fix: sort numeric metadata values numerically in get_metadata_field_unique_values
items.body:
### Related Issues

- N/A — no issue reports this. Found while reading `get_metadata_field_unique_values` against the
  `GetMetadataFieldUniqueValuesTest` mixin, which documents pagination over "a stable ordering".

### Proposed Changes

`InMemoryDocumentStore.get_metadata_field_unique_values` collects unique values keyed by
`(type(value).__name__, hashable_value)` and then ordered them by their string form:

```python
sorted_keys = sorted(unique_values, key=lambda k: (str(unique_values[k]), k[0]))
```

That is fine for keyword fields, but it is not monotonic for numbers — and the result is sliced by
`from_`/`size`:

```python
store.get_metadata_field_unique_values("n", from_=0, size=2)  # ([1, 10], 4)
store.get_metadata_field_unique_values("n", from_=2, size=2)  # ([2, 33], 4)
```

The second-smallest value `2` lands on page 2 while `10` is on page 1, so the page a caller receives
is not the page the ordering implies.

This sorts numbers numerically and keeps non-numbers ordered by their string form. The type name still
breaks ties, so `1` and `1.0` — which are distinct entries — keep a stable relative order across calls.

Scope: `InMemoryDocumentStore` only. The mixin in `haystack/testing/document_store.py` is shared with
the other document stores, so its pagination test keeps using a string field.

### How did you test it?

- Added `test_get_metadata_field_unique_values_sorts_numbers_numerically` to
  `test/document_stores/test_in_memory.py`; it asserts the full order and both pages.
- Reverted the ordering line locally and re-ran it: fails with
  `assert [1, 10, 2, 33] == [1, 2, 10, 33]`.
- Full file: `396 passed, 8 skipped`.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on both changed files: clean.

### Notes for the reviewer

- `#13071` also touches `count_unique_metadata_by_filter` in this file, but it changes the dedup key
  and does not overlap with the ordering line.

- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

items.title: fix(locate): deliver WorkBuddy's user files to the root its app launches from
items.body:
## What this fixes

`#1290` sends WorkBuddy's user-scope skills to `.workbuddy-ai/` whenever that directory exists, reading it as "5.7+ moved its runtime there, and the old root is an unread leftover". The two roots belong to two apps, not to two generations of one: `.workbuddy/` is WorkBuddy's data root, `.workbuddy-ai/` is WorkBuddy AI's — a separate install with its own `WorkBuddyAI.exe` and its own update channel — and uninstalling either one leaves its root behind. Presence therefore names neither root reliably, and half the delivery lands where the running app never looks.

The live root is the one whose `last-launch.json` is newer: each app rewrites that file in the root it starts from. This PR reads both records and follows the newer one. When neither root has a record, it keeps the old presence rule unchanged.

## Measured, not reasoned

Real CLI, `scope: user`, both roots present, team repo carrying one skill, one rule and one MCP server. Before = `main`, after = this branch:

| HOME shape | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `.workbuddy` launched 11-06, `.workbuddy-ai` 11-02 (this machine) | skills → `.workbuddy-ai`, rules + MCP → `.workbuddy` | all three → `.workbuddy` |
| `.workbuddy-ai` launched 11-02, `.workbuddy` 10-27 | skills → `.workbuddy-ai`, rules + MCP → `.workbuddy` | all three → `.workbuddy-ai` |
| no `last-launch.json` in either root | skills → `.workbuddy-ai`, rules + MCP → `.workbuddy` | all three → `.workbuddy-ai` |

The `before` column is the defect in one line: on every machine one half of the delivery goes to the root the app does not read. In row 1 — this machine — the 11 skills the app actually loads sit in `.workbuddy/skills` while teamai writes to `.workbuddy-ai/skills`, which holds migration markers and nothing else.

## Why rules and agents may move now

`#1290` left rules, agents and MCP on `.workbuddy/` because their write path had no confirmed evidence, and that refusal was right. The evidence is in the 5.9.3 build (`app.asar`):

| descriptor | how the engine resolves it | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `rules.user` | `loadProjectRules` → `collect(resolveUserConfigDir('rules', userConfigDir), 'user')` | `<configDir>/rules` — moves to `source` |
| `agents.user` | `loadProjectAgents` → `collect(resolveUserConfigDir('agents', userConfigDir), 'user')` | `<configDir>/agents` — moves to `source` |
| `agents.project` | the project loader has no call site in the build | stays `assumed` |

`resolveUserConfigDir(leaf, dir)` is `join(dir ?? configDir, leaf)`, and the call sites pass no explicit dir, so every one of these leaves hangs off the app's own data root — which is the thing that differs per product. The engine's data-root list holds `.workbuddy` and `.workbuddy-ai` side by side, and each app writes its own files there: `~/.workbuddy/mcp.json` (301 B, 11-04) and `~/.workbuddy-ai/mcp.json` (253 B, 11-03) are both present, both edited separately. A shared config dir does not produce that.

**The one thing I could not read:** WorkBuddy AI's own asar. That install is gone from this machine and only its root remains, so "AI's config dir is `.workbuddy-ai`" is inferred from the two `mcp.json` files above rather than read out of the AI build. Anyone who still has the AI install can settle it with one grep of `resolveUserConfigDir`; if AI turns out to read `<WorkBuddy root>/rules`, the rules move is wrong and should be dropped while the skills half stays.

## What changes

- **`types.ts`** — `applyWorkBuddyGeneration` → `applyWorkBuddyLiveRoot`. In user scope it moves `skills`, `mcp`, `userScope.rules` and `userScope.agents`; each value moves only while it still holds its default, so a team override survives. Project scope still moves `skills` alone. `settings` is deliberately untouched: hooks are the other half of #1273.
- **`tools.ts`** — `rules.user` and `agents.user` evidence `assumed` → `source`; the descriptor comment now records two products instead of two generations. `agents.project` keeps `assumed` with the reason.
- **`locate.ts`** — the install gate and the read/declare paths ask the same `liveWorkbuddyRoot`, so what `doctor` and `status` read is what `pull` writes. Every filesystem read still goes through `Host`.
- **`doctor.ts`** — rules, team instructions, agents and MCP are no longer reported as held on a `.workbuddy-ai/` machine; only hooks are, which is what pull actually does. That flips the silent-green case #1273 reports: doctor used to call every surface delivered while they sat in the root the app does not read.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**, `docs/guide/sharing.md`, `docs/guide/zh-CN/sharing.md` — the same correction in prose.

## Testing

- Real CLI, two builds, three HOME shapes, `pull` only: the table above. The probe scrubs every tool-home environment variable and asserts no path outside its fixture changed.
- `locate-workbuddy.test.ts` 19 passed, `workbuddy-generation.test.ts` 27 passed — 46 total, including both roots for `rules`, `agents` and `mcp` in user scope, and the fail-closed case for project scope.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `oxlint` 0 warnings / 0 errors on the four source files.
- The failures this platform already has (`doctor-delivery`, parts of `instruction-targets`, `tools/types`) fail identically on an unmodified `main` checkout — checked file by file.

For #1273, not closing it: hooks are the other half.

items.title: fix(cli)!: exit 1 when teamai remove removes nothing
items.body:
## Problem

`teamai remove` prints why it could not remove, then exits 0. A script or a CI job that chains the next step on it reads a refusal — or a removal that never reached the team — as done.

Measured on this branch's parent with the real CLI, on a `provider: git` fixture (one rule, one skill, one MCP server):

| command | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `remove nosuchtype foo` | 0 | **1** |
| `remove skills nosuchskill` | 0 | **1** |
| `remove skills nosuchskill --dry-run` | 0 | **1** |
| `remove rules beta` (succeeds) | 0 | 0 |
| `remove rules beta --dry-run` (succeeds) | 0 | 0 |
| `roles add newrole --namespaces newrole` (succeeds) | 0 | 0 |

Six paths bailed out without setting the code, in a file that already set it in five other places — `refuseUnrefreshedRemoval`, the placement-record catch, and the ambiguous-name branch all did. So the contract existed and these were missed, not decided:

- an unsupported resource type, and a call with no names (24, 30);
- a name no file matches — it lists the available names and exits 0 (247);
- a handler that deleted no file (313);
- a push that failed (360);
- a branch pushed but no pull request opened (348).

The last one is also the gap `roles` / `projects` edits had: `pushManifestChange` wrote the manifest, pushed the branch, and treated a null from `createPrWithFallback` as nothing to report. The branch carries the change and nothing reviews it.

## Breaking

These are exit codes a script reads, so the title carries `!` and the CHANGELOG entry sits at the top of `### 💥 Breaking Changes`, not in `### Changed` where I first put it:

- `teamai remove` exits 1 on the six paths above, where it exited 0;
- `teamai roles` / `teamai projects` `add`, `update`, `remove` and `set` exit 1 when the branch is pushed and no pull request opens.

A job that chained on those commands now stops on a refusal instead of continuing. Nothing else about the commands changes: the same lines are printed, and the exit code is the only new signal.

## What "no pull request" means

Three attempts at this line were wrong. Two of them shipped, one to each e2e file.

The first was `if (!prUrl)`. A provider that reaches only git refuses `createPullRequest` outright, so `createPrWithFallback` answers null on **every** `provider: git` push — by configuration, not by failure. `e2e/remove-mcp-namespaces.test.ts` caught it: three passing removals went red.

The second read the provider's `pullRequests` marker: `getProvider(...).pullRequests !== null`. Wrong twice over.

- `e2e/remove-delivered-record-1577.test.ts` caught it on the shard-2 runner: three removals went red with `expected 1 to be +0`. Its fixture sets `provider: tgit` but `repo:` and the remote are both a path under `/tmp`, which that provider does not parse; the fallback answers null there without anything having failed.
- The review caught the other half: `cnb` keeps `pullRequests` null because it cannot **list** a branch's open request, while `createPullRequest` still runs `cnb pulls post-pull`. A failed `cnb` push of a removal reported success. That marker answers a different question — how delivery finds an existing request before opening one — and reading it as "opens none" was my error, not a property of `cnb`.

The line that holds asks two questions, both in `providerOpensPullRequests` (`push.ts`):

- does the provider open them at all — `provider.name !== 'git'`, since generic git is the one provider that refuses to. This is the check `promotion-publish.ts:65` already makes before its own `createPrWithFallback`, and `init.ts:2137`, `source.ts:423` and `push.ts:442` make it too;
- does a repo come out of the same two inputs the fallback parses, the team's `repo` and then the checkout's remote.

Everything else that answers null is a pull request that should have opened and did not.

`provider-opens-pull-requests.test.ts` pins all of it: the git provider, the path-only checkout, the bare `owner/repo` the fallback accepts, the member-over-team provider precedence, and `cnb`, which opens a request it cannot list.

## Not a capability flag

The honest contract would be `opensPullRequests` on `GitProvider`, declared per provider so the compiler asks the question whenever one is added. I did not put it here: it means a field on the interface plus a line in each of the six providers, which turns an exit-code fix into a provider-contract change. `name !== 'git'` is what the call sites above already do, and it reads correctly for `cnb`. If you want the flag, I will open it separately and migrate all of them at once.

## Found, not fixed

`teamai push` has the same null handling at `push.ts:945` and `push.ts:2742`: on `provider: git` it sets exit 1 and returns `'pr-failed'` on every push, even though the branch was pushed. Measured on the same fixture:

```
exit=1  push --all with a new local skill
         √ Pushed branch teamai/push/probe-user/20221105-222143
         × Failed to create PR: Invalid Git repo URL (...)
```

That is older than this branch and reaches the push webhook (a `'pr-failed'` return does not fire it), so I left it alone. Fixing it here would make this PR about `push` as well as `remove`, and the webhook change needs your call. Say the word and I will open it separately.

## Checks

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `oxlint --type-aware --deny-warnings` 0 warnings / 0 errors on 1735 files; `scripts/check-docs.mjs` passes.
- `remove-command.test.ts` 17 cases, `manifest-edit.test.ts` 10, `provider-opens-pull-requests.test.ts` 8, plus `roles-init-refresh.test.ts` and `index-not-initialized.test.ts`: 44 pass, the new ones failing on the parent.
- `e2e/remove-delivered-record-1577.test.ts`: 7 passing — including the three the shard-2 runner failed before the second question was added.
- `e2e/remove-mcp-namespaces.test.ts`: 4 passing, 3 failing — and the parent fails the same 3, with the same assertion: `onBranch` runs `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)'` through `execSync`, which goes through `cmd.exe` on Windows and passes the single quotes to git, so the branch name arrives as `'teamai/push/e2e/...'`. Nothing to do with this change, and green on Linux CI.
- The real-CLI table above is produced by `dist-base` and `dist-head` built from the two trees, with the branch name checked for the new symbol so the two cannot be confused.

Rebased onto `a4ceb72a` (`#1739`, `#1742`), with the CHANGELOG line re-applied on top of theirs.

No `Closes`: there is no issue for this. It is the same audit as #1731, one command family further.

items.title: fix(recall): flag a skill in --update-quality and pick learnings by topic
items.body:
## What

`teamai recall maintenance --update-quality` could never flag a skill, and the learnings it attached to a draft were the team's most-opened entries rather than ones about the same subject. Both live in `src/maintenance/quality-update.ts`.

## Why

**A skill vote id names a directory, not a file.** The search index records a skill's id as its bare name (`collectSkillEntries` writes `filename = <name>.md`, and `voteKey` drops the extension), while the file is `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` or `skills/<namespace>/<name>/SKILL.md`. `resolveDocPath` joined the id onto `skills/` as `<id>.md`, which never exists, so the entry was dropped at `if (!entryPath) continue` — with no log line, which is why nothing looked wrong. Docs and rules were unaffected because their ids already carry the namespace.

**The adopted learnings were not about anything in particular.** `findRelatedAdoptedLearnings` summed `upvoted_count` per doc, sorted, took the top `limit`, and only then dropped the entries that were not learnings. Five popular docs therefore used every slot, and nothing compared a candidate with the entry — while the prompt tells the model to "Incorporate relevant insights from the adopted learnings above".

## The change

- `resolveEntry` returns the entry's path and its type together. The type comes from the directory that matched instead of `entryPath.includes('/docs/')`, which is false for every path on Windows, where `path.join` yields backslashes — every entry there was reported as `[unknown]`.
- `findSkillFile` tries the flat layout, then each namespace directory. A vote id that is not a single path segment is refused, so a hand-edited id cannot walk out of `skills/`.
- An id that clears every threshold and still matches no file is named in one warning instead of vanishing. A votes file also holds learning ids, which are not in `knowledgeDirs` by design, so the list is collected and summarised rather than logged entry by entry.
- `findRelatedAdoptedLearnings` filters to learnings first, then ranks by the words the entry's name, title and tags share with the learning's name, then slices. A learning that shares no word is left out rather than padding the prompt.
- A namespaced learning's vote id now matches its file on Windows: the listing joins with `path.sep` while the id keeps the `/` the index wrote.

## Real CLI, same fixture, two builds

Fixture: a team repo holding `docs/guide.md`, `skills/flat-skill/SKILL.md` and `skills/pay/refund-skill/SKILL.md`, with two members' v2 votes giving each of the three 5 recalls, plus one id (`gone-skill`) that has no file behind it.

Before, on `main` at `df06b5a0`:

```
ℹ Found 1 entry(ies) recalled often but rarely adopted:
ℹ   - [unknown] guide: recalled 5x by 2 users, adopted 0x
```

After:

```
⚠ 1 entry(ies) reached the threshold but no file matched under docs/, rules/ or skills/: gone-skill
ℹ Found 3 entry(ies) recalled often but rarely adopted:
ℹ   - [skills] refund-skill: recalled 5x by 2 users, adopted 0x
ℹ   - [skills] flat-skill: recalled 5x by 2 users, adopted 0x
ℹ   - [docs] guide: recalled 5x by 2 users, adopted 0x
```

Both skill layouts appear, the ids that cannot be placed are named, and the type is no longer `unknown` on Windows.

## Tests

- `src/__tests__/maintenance-quality-update.test.ts` (new, 13 cases): both skill layouts, flat preferred when a skill exists in both, a path-shaped id refused, the warning, staying quiet below the threshold, a related learning surviving five more-popular docs, an unrelated learning left out, closer-first ranking, a namespaced learning, and the votes files left on disk.
- `src/__tests__/e2e/recall-maintenance-skills-1735.test.ts` (new): the fixture above, run against the built CLI.

Reverse check: with `src/maintenance/quality-update.ts` restored to `main`, 10 of the 13 unit cases fail. The three that pass assert an absence — `does not walk out of skills/`, `stays quiet below the threshold`, `leaves the votes files on disk`.

`tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint --type-aware --deny-warnings` (0 warnings and 0 errors on 1736 files) and `scripts/check-docs.mjs` pass on this branch.

## Scope

The second half changes behaviour: a draft with no related learning now gets none, where it used to get the most-opened entries. That is what the issue asks for. If you would rather keep the old filling, the first half stands on its own — say so and I will drop the second.

Addresses #1735; I left it unlinked so a merge does not close it if you take only the first half.

items.title: docs: document that XLSXToDocument row numbering assumes the pandas positional index
items.body:
### Related Issues

- N/A

### Proposed Changes

`XLSXToDocument` numbers the rows of the output table from 1 so that they match the Excel row numbers:

    df.index = df.index + 1

That only holds when pandas assigns the positional index. Supporting every combination of `read_excel_kwargs` in the converter is out of scope, so this documents the limitation in the `read_excel_kwargs` docstring instead, following the `CSVDocumentSplitter` wording.

The added paragraph states that:

- options that shift the rows or replace the index, such as `skiprows` or `index_col`, make the numbering inaccurate;
- a source whose `index_col` holds non-numeric values is skipped;
- the conversion output should be validated on representative inputs when these options are customized.

Behavior is unchanged — the diff is docstring only.

### How did you test it?

No behavior change, so no new test. I checked that the documented behavior is what `main` actually does:

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `index_col` on a string column | 0 documents, warning `can only concatenate str (not "int") to str` |
| `index_col` on a numeric column with a header row | 0 documents, same warning (the header text lands in the index) |
| `index_col` on a numeric column without a header row | rows renumbered `101, 102` → `102, 103` |
| `skiprows=2` | rows numbered from 1 instead of the Excel row numbers 3, 4 |

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` report the same results as on unmodified `main` for this file.

### Notes for the reviewer

- Dropped the test and the release note from the earlier revision; the branch is now a single docstring commit based on `0de7bcdc`.
- The `index_col` failure above is a separate pre-existing defect. Happy to send a follow-up that guards only that case if you'd rather fix it than document it.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] I have signed the [Contributor License Agreement](https://cla-assistant.io/deepset-ai/haystack).

items.title: fix(cli): exit 1 when a roles or projects edit is refused or fails
items.body:
`teamai projects set nosuchproject` prints `✖ Unknown project "nosuchproject". Valid projects: alpha` and then exits **0**. So does every other refusal from `teamai roles` and `teamai projects`, and so does the shared manifest edit when its preview, its worktree or its push cannot be prepared. A script, a hook, or a CI job that runs one of these commands reads a refusal as success, and a push that never opened the pull request leaves the manifest written locally while reporting nothing wrong.

## What I measured

On `main` at b1329c4c, against a throwaway team repo (local bare remote, isolated `HOME`, `teamai.yaml` and both manifests committed), running the built CLI:

| command | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `projects list`, `roles list` | 0 | 0 |
| `projects add beta --namespaces beta` | 0 | 0 |
| `projects set nosuchproject` | **0** | **1** |
| `projects add alpha --namespaces alpha` (duplicate) | **0** | **1** |
| `projects add gamma --namespaces ' '` | **0** | **1** |
| `projects update alpha` (nothing to change) | **0** | **1** |
| `projects update ghost --name X` | **0** | **1** |
| `projects update alpha --remove-namespaces alpha` | **0** | **1** |
| `projects remove ghost` | **0** | **1** |
| `roles set ghost` | **0** | **1** |
| `roles add hai --namespaces hai` (duplicate) | **0** | **1** |
| `roles add qa --namespaces ' '` | **0** | **1** |
| `roles update hai` (nothing to change) | **0** | **1** |
| `roles update ghost --add-namespaces x` | **0** | **1** |
| `roles update hai --remove-namespaces common,hai` | **0** | **1** |
| `roles remove ghost` | **0** | **1** |

The four commands that succeed exit 0 on both sides, so this changes the refusals only.

## Why the code, not a new policy

The repository already reads "refused" as "failed" everywhere else, and twice inside the files this PR touches:

- `roles-cmd.ts` already sets `process.exitCode = 1` when `roles set` refuses a team-assigned role.
- `runManifestEdit` already does it for a dirty preview and a detached clone; the other two branches of the same `catch` did not.
- `codebase-cmd.ts` and `cache-cmd.ts` set it for their own refusals, `2` for a bad flag value.
- The update branch reached the same conclusion in #1703: a manual `update` that fails should not exit 0.

So the 25 refusals here are a missing line, not a decision someone made.

## What changed

- **`src/roles-cmd.ts`** — 15 bail-out paths: an unreadable manifest in `list`/`set`/`add`/`remove`/`update`, an unknown primary or additional role, a missing namespace, a duplicate id, a missing id, the last role, a removal that would empty a role, and a call with nothing to update.
- **`src/projects-cmd.ts`** — 10: no manifest, an unknown project on `set`/`update`/`remove`, an unreadable or invalid manifest, a missing namespace, a duplicate id, a call with nothing to update, and a removal that would empty a project.
- **`src/manifest-edit.ts`** — the edit's `catch` now sets the code once after it has reported, instead of only on two of its three branches, and a failed push in `pushManifestChange` sets it too. That last one is the case that matters most: the manifest is already saved at that point, so a silent 0 says the pull request exists when it does not.

Nothing else moves: the messages, the order they print in, and every path that already succeeded are untouched.

## Tests

- `src/__tests__/roles-admin-exit-code.test.ts` (new) — 15 cases, one per refusal above, plus a success that stays 0.
- `src/__tests__/projects-cmd.test.ts` — 12 cases on the same pattern, against the existing fixtures.
- `src/__tests__/manifest-edit.test.ts` — the two existing failure cases now assert the code, and a new pair covers a failed push and a push that goes through.

Each case resets `process.exitCode` in `afterEach`, since it is global state that would otherwise leak into the next case and into vitest's own status.

Reverse check: with the three source files restored, 28 of the 56 cases in these three files fail — the 14 role refusals, the 11 project refusals and the 3 edit failures — and every success case still passes.

`tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint --type-aware --deny-warnings` and `scripts/check-docs.mjs` all pass on this branch.

## The dry run

`e2e/dry-run-git-previews-900.test.ts` pinned `code = 0` on two `roles add` previews that go on to report `Role "…" already exists` (lines 417 and 502). A dry run exists to answer what the real run would do — one of those tests is named "matches the real pull" — so a preview that finds the role taken should exit the way `roles add` does, or a script cannot use it as a pre-check. I changed those two assertions to 1; the preview content they assert is untouched, and the other cases in that file pass unchanged, `roles init` on an existing manifest included, which still exits 0 because there the goal is already met.

If you would rather keep `--dry-run` at 0 whatever it finds, say so and I will scope the 25 role and project bail-outs to a real run instead. The three `manifest-edit` failures would keep their code either way.

## Not in this PR

- `roles init`'s interactive "no roles defined" bail-out takes the same line for consistency, but reaching it needs a TTY and no test drives it. Happy to drop that one line if you would rather keep every change covered.
- `createPrWithFallback` reports a pull request it could not open without setting a code either. That is `push`'s surface rather than a manifest edit's, so it belongs in its own change.
- #1728 does not touch any of these files.

items.title: docs: clarify that word_count_threshold counts whitespace-separated words, not tokens
items.body:
## What

Documentation-only change to `LostInTheMiddleRanker`: the docs now spell out what `word_count_threshold` actually counts. No behaviour change.

## Why

`word_count_threshold` is computed with `str.split()`, so it budgets whitespace-separated chunks, not model tokens. Users reasonably read "words" as a proxy for the downstream context window, but a URL, a hash, or a code expression counts as one word no matter how many tokens a tokenizer splits it into, and code-heavy or non-Latin text needs noticeably more tokens per word than English prose. A threshold sized for a model's context window can therefore still overflow it.

@julian-risch offered exactly this follow-up in #11351:

> If you have a suggestion how to improve the docstring to make this limitation more clear, feel free to open a PR.

## Changes

- `__init__`: the paragraph describing the threshold now states the counting unit.

items.title: fix(update): exit non-zero when a manual update fails to install
items.body:
**What**

`teamai update` exited `0` when the install failed. `doUpdate()` warned, persisted, and returned normally, so a script could not tell a failed update from a successful one.

`doUpdate()` now returns `UpdateOutcome`:

- `failed` — only when the install itself threw (the three branches of the `catch`)
- `ok` — every other exit: no update available, a policy or layout refusal, a concurrent update, a declined prompt

`update()` turns `failed` into `process.exitCode = 1`. The message is left exactly as it was (already on stderr), so the only visible change is the exit status. The hook path ignores the return value, and its detached child's status is discarded anyway (`stdio: ['pipe', 'ignore', 'ignore']`).

**Boundary**

Deliberate refusals (linked checkout, Volta image, vendored layout, another update already running) still exit `0`: each prints an actionable message and none of them is an error. Say if you want those non-zero as well — it is a one-line change in `update()`.

**Tests**

`src/__tests__/update.test.ts`:

- `doUpdate()` reports `failed` and `ok` to its caller
- `update()` sets `process.exitCode = 1` on a failed install, and leaves it untouched on success (both restore the previous value)

`npx vitest run src/__tests__/update.test.ts` → 84 passed. Mutating `=== 'failed'` to `=== 'ok'` makes exactly the two exit-code tests fail. `tsc --noEmit` and `oxlint --type-aware --deny-warnings` are clean.

**Real-CLI verification**

Built with `tsup` and installed into a fake npm global layout (`<tmp>/prefix/node_modules/teamai-cli`), then `node <pkg>/dist/cli.js update` with `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` on a temp home against a local HTTP registry.

Failing install (registry advertises `99.0.0`, 404s the tarball):

- `main` (`c01d5f8`, built the same way) → `exit 0`
- this branch → `exit 1`

The terminal output is unchanged between the two: the same `[WARN] Update failed: … npm error code E404 …` line, only the status differs.

Already up to date (registry advertises the installed `0.22.0`) on this branch → `exit 0`, `ℹ Already up to date (v0.22.0)`.

Refs #1702

items.title: fix(update): persist self-update failures to debug.log
items.body:
**What**

`doUpdate()` reported a failed install only through `log.warn`, which never reaches `debug.log`. Two sites:

- the install-failure `catch` — all three branches (`src/update.ts:1065`)
- the post-install check that finds the running install still on the old version (`src/update.ts:1037`)

Both now pair `log.persist` with the warning, the same way the three "cannot update in place" exits a few lines above already do (`src/update.ts:946`, `:964`, `:980`).

**Why it matters**

The update handler is registered `background: true` (`src/hook-handlers.ts:1423`), so it runs in the detached child created by `spawnPlainDetached`:

```ts
stdio: ['pipe', 'ignore', 'ignore'],   // src/hook-dispatch-cli.ts:132
```

That child's stdout and stderr go nowhere. `log.warn` writes to stderr only and returns early in silent mode (`src/utils/logger.ts:172`); only `persist`, `error` and `debug` append to `~/.teamai/debug.log`. So when an auto-update dies inside the Stop hook, nothing is recorded anywhere — which is the log #1685 asks reporters to send.

Scope: this changes nothing about what the update does, it only makes a failure observable. The root cause in #1685 (npm leaving `.teamai-cli-*` behind on Windows) is untouched.

**Tests**

`src/__tests__/update.test.ts` — the two existing failure tests now assert `persist` next to `warn`, plus one new case for an unclassified error and the same assertion on the staleness check. The concurrent-update skip asserts it does *not* persist (a second update running is not a failure).

- `npx vitest run src/__tests__/update.test.ts` → 80 passed
- reverting `src/update.ts` to `main` makes exactly those 4 tests fail
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `oxlint --type-aware --deny-warnings` clean

Built with `tsup`, installed into a fake npm global layout (`<tmp>/prefix/node_modules/teamai-cli`), then ran `node <pkg>/dist/cli.js update` with `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` pointed at a temp home. ```
2026-11-04T01:40:36.383Z [DEBUG] bundled runtime: git already resolves on PATH; leaving it alone
```

The `Update failed: … npm error code E404 …` text reached stderr and nothing else.

This PR, same scenario:

```
2026-11-04T01:40:09.257Z [WARN] Update failed: Command failed: <node> <npm-cli.js> install -g teamai-cli --prefix=<tmp>\prefix --registry=http://127.0.0.1:52417
npm error code E404
npm error 404 Not Found - GET http://127.0.0.1:52417/teamai-cli/-/teamai-cli-99.0.0.tgz - Not found

npm error 404 tarball, folder, http url, or git url.

items.title: fix(app): ignore duplicate index tasks for ready documents

labels.name: pr/awaiting-review

items.body:
## AgentScope Version

2.0.12dev

## Description

Fixes #3650.

`IndexWorker.process` guards concurrent work with a processing lease, but that lease only excludes workers that are indexing *right now*. Once a delivery reaches `ready` it releases the lease, so a duplicate entry in the durable index queue acquires a fresh lease and runs the whole pipeline again. Because the pipeline calls `delete_document` before generating new embeddings, a transient failure on that second run destroys chunks that were already healthy and leaves the document in `error`, with no reindex requested by anyone.

This adds an admission check at the top of `_run_pipeline`: a document whose status is already `ready` is skipped, so a duplicate delivery does nothing at all.

The check is deliberately narrow. `error` is **not** treated as terminal, so a redelivery of a failed document is still reprocessed, and an explicit re-index keeps working through the existing status reset to `pending`. The scope matches the expected behaviour recorded in the issue.

**Tests** (`tests/index_worker_duplicate_task_test.py`, real `IndexWorker` over storage, blob and vector-store doubles):

- a delivery after `ready` leaves status, chunk count, recorded transitions, embedding calls and vector-store writes exactly as they were
- a failing embedding backend cannot degrade a `ready` document through a duplicate delivery — this is the reported damage, and on unmodified `main` it ends in `error` with zero chunks
- ignoring a duplicate still releases the lease it acquired
- a `pending` document is still indexed normally
- an `error` document is still re-indexed

Also adds the top-level `status` field to the record stub in `tests/index_worker_content_type_test.py`; the pipeline now reads it, and `KnowledgeDocumentRecord` really does carry it at the top level.

Verified locally: the two defect tests fail on unmodified `main` and pass with the fix, the three "real work still runs" tests pass on both, and on the pristine base the two defect tests fail and every other test in `index_worker_lease_test`, `index_worker_main_test` and `index_worker_content_type_test` passes unchanged (6 passed + 2 subtests before and after), and the failure set of `rag_parser_test` and `service_enqueue_index_task_test` is byte-identical before and after (71, all pre-existing: `rag_parser` needs optional document backends and the enqueue tests need a Redis that answers `eval`, neither of which works on this Windows box -- both reproduce on an untouched checkout of the base commit). `black`, `flake8`, `pylint` (10.00/10) and `mypy` are clean on the touched files; the rest is left to CI.

items.title: fix(import): recognise an origin-less --dir checkout by a hash of its git root
items.body:
## What

`--incremental` promises to re-extract only the files changed since the last import (`docs/guide/knowledge.md:151`). For a `--dir` checkout with no `origin` remote it never did: every run was a full extraction. Once the baseline does match, a second gap shows up — the re-import replaces the curated docs, because `sameRepository` (`src/import-codebase.ts:74`, added by #1417) decides that by `repoUrl`, which an origin-less checkout does not have.

This is gap 3 of #1422. Gap 4 is #1425, gap 1 is #1417. Gap 2 (two checkouts with the same basename sharing one evidence directory) is **not** fixed here: they still share `evidence/code/<slug>/`. What changes is that the second checkout no longer inherits the first one's curated docs.

**Ordering with #1440.** That PR, opened after this one, also rewrites `sameRepository` — as `publishedSource` — and it refuses an origin-less import over evidence published by a remote, where this PR replaces the docs. Whichever lands first, the other needs a rebase and one test changes: `replaces the docs when the published manifest names a remote` asserts today's replace, and refusing is the stricter reading, so I would drop my version of that case rather than theirs. The overlap is described on #1440.

## Reproduction

`main@97a762ce`, the real `extractCodebase` (no mocks), two temp git repos that differ only by `git remote add origin`:

| checkout | manifest keys after run 1 | run 2, after editing one file |
|---|---|---|
| no `origin` | `version,lastScan,project,files,sourceSubdir,headSha` | `no matching source baseline, running full extraction`, **2 files scanned** |
| with `origin` | the same plus `repoUrl,repoIdentity` | `incremental: 1 files changed, 0 deleted`, **1 file scanned** |

The two rows share every input except that one config line, so the difference is the remote and nothing else.

## Why

- `manifestMatchesSource` required `source.repoIdentity` (`src/codebase-extract.ts:609`).
- `sourceRepositoryMetadata` returned only `{sourceSubdir}` when the checkout had no remote URL (`:650`).
- So `incrementalBaselineMatches` (`:700`) was false on every run, and the run printed the fallback notice.

## Fix

For a checkout with no remote identity, record `sha256(realpath(git root))` as `localRootHash` and compare it in `manifestMatchesSource`; compare it in `sameRepository` as well, so the docs carry over too.

It is a separate field rather than a value written into `repoIdentity` because `manifestRepoIdentity` in `src/codebase-freshness.ts:64` feeds `repoIdentity` into remote-versus-remote matching — a filesystem path stored there would make freshness compare a path against URLs.

## What changed since the reviews

Both review points were right, including the part of my rationale that was wrong.

**[P1] `localRoot` is no longer written for a checkout that has a remote.** `sourceRepositoryMetadata` now returns it only on the path where `remoteUrl` is empty, so `repoIdentity` identifies a remote checkout and nothing else is added to a manifest the team commits. The reason I gave for writing it everywhere — "dropping an `origin` afterwards does not throw away a usable baseline" — does not hold, and the measurement confirms your reading: `manifestMatchesSource` refuses a manifest that names a remote for an origin-less checkout (`:638-639`), so removing `origin` after a remote import is a full run either way.

**[P2] The value is a hash, not the raw path.** `sha256(realpath(git root))` matches exactly the same pairs of runs, and `source-manifest.json` no longer carries `/Users/<name>/…`.

**`sameRepository` handles the origin-less case.** Now that #1417 is in, comparing `repoUrl` alone leaves an origin-less checkout with no identity, so its curated docs were replaced on every re-import. Both sides blank now fall through to the same `localRootHash` and `sourceSubdir` comparison, and a manifest without the hash (written by an older CLI) is treated as "not the same source" rather than as a match.

**[P1, bot review] Two subdirectories of one origin-less repo no longer share curated docs.** `service-a/svc` and `service-b/svc` of one repository hash to the same git root, so the hash on its own called them the same source and handed the first one's docs to the second — the exact case in the review. `sameRepository` now requires the recorded `sourceSubdir` to be equal too, which is the condition `manifestMatchesSource` already applied to the baseline. Both values are in the manifest the review pointed at; the real-CLI run below is that scenario end to end.

## Compatibility

- A manifest written before this change has no `localRootHash`, so each origin-less codebase pays **one** more full extraction and increments from then on.
- Moving or copying a checkout produces a different hash, so the new path counts as a new source: `--incremental` falls back to one full extraction, and a re-import through `import --dir` replaces the curated `docs/` instead of carrying it over. That is the safe direction. The alternative — falling back to the slug — is the same-basename collision this PR refuses to reintroduce, and a moved checkout cannot be told apart from "another checkout with the same name"; only one of those two readings is ever safe, and the basename is the unsafe one. So a move costs one full run and the AI-written docs, and the trade-off is deliberate, not an oversight.
- Remote-backed checkouts behave exactly as before, and their manifests do not gain a new field.

## Tests

`src/__tests__/codebase-incremental-no-origin.test.ts`, nine cases against real git repos:

1. reuses the baseline of the same checkout (the bug);
2. records no root hash when the checkout has an origin;
3. refuses a baseline that names a remote the checkout does not have;
4. refuses a baseline extracted from a different directory;
5. refuses a baseline written before `localRootHash` existed;
6. carries the curated docs across a re-import of the same checkout;
7. replaces the docs of a different checkout that shares the basename;
8. replaces the docs of another subdirectory of the same origin-less repo — the bot-review case: same hash, `service-a/svc` then `service-b/svc`, and the case first asserts that re-importing `service-a/svc` still keeps its docs, so it cannot pass by never carrying anything;
9. replaces the docs when the published manifest names a remote.

Three reverse arms, each reverting one part of the fix and leaving the tests intact:

| reverted | fails | passes |
|---|---|---|
| `sameRepository` back to `main`'s version | 6, 8 | 1–5, 7, 9 |
| the `localRootHash` write only | 1, 6, 8 | 2–5, 7, 9 |
| the `sourceSubdir` comparison only | 8 | 1–7, 9 |

Case 8 fails in all three because it needs the whole chain: a hash that matches, the write that records it, and the directory check that tells two codebases apart. The others fail only where their own part is removed, and 3–5, 7, 9 are a guard rather than a restatement of the fix.

## Real-CLI verification

`npm run build` (tsup), then the built CLI against a git repo with **no remotes at all** (`git remote -v` empty), inside a single-mode team repo:

```
$ node dist/index.js import --dir .../verify/a/svc3 --skip-enrich
[extract] svc3 complete
  Files: 3

$ node dist/index.js import --dir .../verify/a/svc3 --incremental --skip-enrich
[extract] incremental: 1 files changed, 0 deleted
[extract] svc3 complete
  Files: 1
```

The baseline published by run 1, read back from `teamwiki/evidence/code/svc3/source-manifest.json`:

```
localRootHash = bedb8b90b9596586a1f57626933fa33f2bd6162a8f9ad5994bd569730d34c6d3
```

No `localRoot`, no `repoUrl`, no `repoIdentity`, and no path anywhere in the file. `sha256(realpath(.../verify/a/svc3))` computed independently from the shell gives the same digest, so the field is a hash of the checkout and not of something else.

Two subdirectories of one origin-less repo, which is the case the bot review raised — one repository with `service-a/svc` and `service-b/svc`, imported under the basename slug both of them derive:

```
=== RUN 1: import repo/service-a/svc ===
  manifest: sourceSubdir="service-a/svc" localRootHash=b1bd9738ef6de7d4… repoUrl=undefined
=== RUN 2: import repo/service-a/svc again ===
  manifest: sourceSubdir="service-a/svc" localRootHash=b1bd9738ef6de7d4… repoUrl=undefined
  curated doc KEPT
=== RUN 3: import repo/service-b/svc (same basename, same git root) ===
  manifest: sourceSubdir="service-b/svc" localRootHash=b1bd9738ef6de7d4… repoUrl=undefined
  curated doc GONE -> replaced with service-b's own evidence
```

Same hash in all three runs, so the hash genuinely identifies the repository and not the codebase; the subdirectory is what separates them.

Three more runs with the same binary:

| checkout | result |
|---|---|
| origin-less, curated doc written by hand into `docs/`, then one source file edited | `incremental: 1 files changed`; `docs/curated-by-ai.md` is still there afterwards |
| has `origin` | manifest has `repoUrl` + `repoIdentity` and **no** `localRootHash` |
| had `origin`, then `git remote remove origin`, then `--incremental` | `no matching source baseline, running full extraction`, 2 files — dropping an origin does not reuse the old baseline |
| the same checkout copied to another path under the same basename, then `--incremental` | `no matching source baseline, running full extraction`, 3 files; `localRootHash` becomes `24cb91f7…`, which is `sha256(realpath(new path))` computed separately, and the curated `docs/` is gone |

The `autoPush failed` line in these runs comes from the stand-in `git@github.com:acme/team.git` origin on the sandbox team repo, not from the source checkout.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors |
| `oxlint --type-aware --deny-warnings --report-unused-disable-directives` | 1336 files, 0 warnings, 0 errors |
| `codebase-incremental-no-origin` + `import-codebase` + `codebase` + `codebase-freshness` | 49 passed, 1 skipped |
| new file alone | 9 passed |

`codebase-reconcile.test.ts` still fails one case on a Windows checkout; it fails identically with `src/codebase-extract.ts` reverted to `main`, so it predates this change. CI covers the rest.

items.title: fix(wecombot): throttle intermediate stream frames in WS mode
items.body:
## 概述 / Overview

With the WeCom AI Bot (`wecombot`) adapter in WebSocket mode, every reply chunk is forwarded to WeCom as its own stream frame.

The long-connection protocol has no server-side refresh callback — the docs are explicit that in long-connection mode 不再有流式刷新回调，开发者需主动推送流式更新内容，直到设置 `finish=true` 结束流式消息 ([protocol reference](https://developer.work.weixin.qq.com/document/path/101463)). Frame pacing is therefore entirely the client's responsibility.

`WecomBotWsClient.push_stream_chunk` currently sends a frame for every chunk whose content changed, with no pacing at all. Since each frame must carry the **complete snapshot** (WeCom replaces the whole bubble on every refresh, as the comment in `push_stream_chunk` notes), a long answer gets re-uploaded once per chunk — total bytes on the wire grow with roughly the square of the answer length.

Concretely: a 3,000-character answer delivered in ~20-character chunks produces ~150 frames carrying ~226,000 characters in total — about 76x the answer itself.

## 更改 / Changes

`src/langbot/libs/wecom_ai_bot_api/ws_client.py` (single file, +27 lines)

- Add a module-level `_STREAM_PUSH_MIN_INTERVAL = 0.3` plus a per-message `_stream_last_push_at` timestamp map.
- In `push_stream_chunk`, skip intermediate frames that arrive inside the interval. The **first frame of a message and the final chunk always go out**, so a reply still starts and ends promptly.
- Release the timestamp at every point where the rest of a message's stream state is released: the final chunk, `_prune_stream_state` (cache eviction), `disconnect`, and both stream tear-down paths in `push_form_pause`.

Dropping intermediate frames is **lossless** here: the runner sends cumulative snapshots, so the next frame already contains everything that was skipped. That is also why this change deliberately leaves the merge logic around `_stream_last_content` untouched — the throttle is a pure bypass switch.

This mirrors the existing throttle in the Discord adapter, which spaces edits out to stay within the platform rate limit (`discord.py`, `_STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL`). Webhook mode needs no equivalent change: `WecomBotClient.push_stream_chunk` only enqueues into an in-process queue and already coalesces slow consumers.

## 更改前后对比 / Before and after

No UI is involved — this is a wire-level pacing change, so the evidence is test output rather than screenshots.

修改前 / Before:

- `tests/unit_tests/platform` had **no coverage of frame pacing**.
- Adding the throttle surfaced one existing test that pinned "one frame per chunk" (`test_wecombot_stream_sends_cumulative_snapshots_to_wecom`, from #2226): **1 failed, 33 passed**.

修改后 / After:

- `tests/unit_tests/platform` (wecombot), run against the repo's own `pytest.ini`: **34 passed**
- `ruff check src tests` across the whole repo: `All checks passed!`
- `ruff format --check` on the changed files: `3 files already formatted`

## 测试 / Tests

New `tests/unit_tests/platform/test_wecombot_stream_throttle.py` (7 tests, same `RecordingClient` style as `test_wecombot_stream_empty_final.py`): first frame always sent; frames inside the interval dropped; delivery resumed once the interval has elapsed; final chunk bypassing the throttle; no content lost when frames are dropped; per-message tracking; state released on finish.

The one existing test that had to be adjusted, and why:

`tests/unit_tests/platform/test_wecombot_template_card.py`: `test_ws_stream_sends_cumulative_snapshots_to_wecom` asserted one frame per chunk. Its subject is cumulative-snapshot semantics, not pacing, so it now takes a `monkeypatch` fixture that sets `_STREAM_PUSH_MIN_INTERVAL` to `0.0`, leaving its assertions untouched. Pacing has its own coverage in the new file. Without that change the suite goes red on this test alone, which is how I found it.

How much of this I could verify locally: this repo declares 77 runtime dependencies (chromadb, qdrant-client, pymilvus, langchain, litellm, boto3, pandas, quart, ...) and installing them was not feasible in my environment. The results above come from loading the real `wecombotevent.py`, `api.py` and `ws_client.py` sources with the third-party imports stubbed — the code under test is the genuine article, and the repo's real `pytest.ini` is used, so `filterwarnings = error::ResourceWarning` and `--strict-markers` are active. What this does **not** cover is the rest of the suite; that is left to CI.

## CI 首轮反馈 / First CI run

The first CI run on this branch failed: `Unit Tests` was red on 3.11 / 3.12 / 3.13 with **5 failed, 3126 passed**. All five failures were in the new `test_wecombot_stream_throttle.py`; **no existing test regressed**.

They were pointing at a real defect in my own change, and it is worth recording why. `push_stream_chunk` used `self._stream_last_push_at.get(msg_id, 0.0)` to mean "nothing sent yet". But `time.monotonic()` has an **arbitrary origin** — on a freshly provisioned runner the raw clock reading is smaller than the interval, so "never sent" was misread as "inside the interval" and the first frame of the message was dropped, taking every following intermediate frame with it.

My local machine masked it: its monotonic clock reads 563,000s, so the same fixture passed there. Shifting `time.monotonic()` to start at 50s reproduces a fresh host locally and makes the five tests fail exactly as CI did.

Fixed in the second commit by checking the entry for `None` explicitly, so the first frame of a message goes out regardless of where the monotonic clock happens to start. Re-verified under the shifted clock, and again against the repo's real `pytest.ini`: **34 passed** both times.

## 上游同步核查 / Upstream drift

This branch was cut from `874eb660`. Master has since moved to `c17ccba1` (243 commits, including the 4.11 integration).

Upstream's only changes to `ws_client.py` in that range are the `TYPE_CHECKING` import move (twice — for `typing` and for `EventLogger`) and a `template_card` payload validation added in `reply_template_card`. Those are disjoint from every hunk in this PR. I replayed the merge locally: all 8 change sites matched uniquely, and the resulting diff against this branch is exactly those three upstream edits. GitHub reports the PR `MERGEABLE`.

## 说明 / Notes

- The interval is a module constant rather than a config key, so this stays a one-file behaviour change with no config-format churn. If you would rather it be tunable, I am happy to wire it into `wecombot.yaml`.
- Refs #2540.

## 检查清单 / Checklist

- [x] 已阅读贡献指引 / Read the [contribution guide](https://github.com/langbot-app/LangBot/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] CLA — 已签署 / signed in [#2564 (comment)](https://github.com/langbot-app/LangBot/pull/2564#issuecomment-5797854300); the bot reports `All contributors have signed the CLA`
- [x] 与项目所有者沟通 / Communicated with the project maintainer — I posted a claim comment on [#2540](https://github.com/langbot-app/LangBot/issues/2540#issuecomment-5796464584) with my intended approach; **no reply yet**, so please treat the design as unconfirmed rather than agreed.
- [x] 已自行测试 / Tested the changes myself — for the wecombot unit tests, as detailed above; the full suite is left to CI.

- `npx vitest run` (full suite): 574 files passed, 1 failed (`workflow-reconciliation.test.ts`, a 15s test timeout under local machine load; no file in this PR touches workflow code).
- Real CLI, real `gh` 2.103.0 behind a local proxy that accepts `CONNECT` and never answers (`HTTPS_PROXY`, isolated `HOME` and `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `GH_TOKEN` set, no `GITHUB_TOKEN`), `teamai import --from-org example-org --skip-import`:

```
exit code = 1 | elapsed = 30.6s | proxy connections = 1
proxy requests = ["CONNECT api.github.com:443 HTTP/1.1"]
whitelist draft unchanged = true
✖ listOrgRepos failed: TimeoutError: gh api /orgs/example-org/repos?per_page=100&page=1 timed out after 30000 ms
```

### Real-CLI record (required by AGENTS.md, since this changes runtime behaviour)

Built, then ran the actual CLI against a stalled `gh`. A local TCP server accepts the proxy `CONNECT` and never answers, so the **real `gh` binary** blocks in the handshake with no deadline of its own — the same shape as a blackholed DNS or a hung corporate proxy, minus network flakiness. `HTTPS_PROXY` points at it; everything else is the normal path (`teamai import --from-org example-org`).

Head (this branch):

```
exit code = 1 | elapsed = 32.4s | proxy connections = 1
× Import from organization [FAILED: listOrgRepos failed: TimeoutError:
  gh api /orgs/example-org/repos?per_page=100&page=1 timed out after 30000 ms]
```

`main` (`157516d4`), with only `gh-org.ts` reverted:

```
exit code = 1 | elapsed = 124.8s | proxy connections = 2
× Import from organization [FAILED: listOrgRepos failed: Error: gh api failed (1):
  Get "https://api.github.com/users/example-org/repos?per_page=100&page=1":
  context deadline exceeded]
```

Note the second line of the `main` record: it is already asking `/users/...`, i.e. it spent a full deadline on `/orgs` and then started over on the fallback.

### Unit-test record

`src/__tests__/gh-org-errors.test.ts` went from 16 to 18 tests (the new case runs against both transports). The batch covering this path:

```
Test Files  1 failed | 15 passed (16)
     Tests  1 failed | 304 passed (305)
```

The single failure is the pre-existing one described at the end of these notes.

### Reverting the fix fails the new test

With `gh-org.ts` reverted to `main` and nothing else changed:

```
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 17 passed (18)
  → expected 'Error' to be 'TimeoutError'
```

The `fetch` half of that table still passes while reverted, which is the intended control: #1381 already fixed that transport.

## Related Issues

Closes #1397

## Notes for Reviewers

**Why passing `timeoutMs` alone is not enough.** `spawnSync` reports a deadline as `status: null` plus `error.code === 'ETIMEDOUT'`. `ghExec` maps that to `{ status: 1, stdout: '', stderr: '' }`, so `ghApiPage` would throw an error whose message is the empty string, and `tryEndpointPrefix` (`page === 1 && allowFallback`) would swallow it and retry `/users` — a second request that stalls identically. Two deadlines instead of one, which is what the `main` record above shows.

So the change has three parts, and all three are needed:

1. `ghExec` reports `timedOut` (additive optional field, both the normal and `inheritStdio` branches);
2. `ghApiPage` turns that into an error named `TimeoutError`, the same name `AbortSignal.timeout()` already produces on the REST path;
3. the `/users` fallback skips a timeout — the guard #1381 added inline for REST is now `isTimeoutError()`, used by both transports, so they cannot drift.

`REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` moved to the top of the pagination section so both transports read the same constant (it was declared below `fetchApiPage`, i.e. after the gh path that now needs it).

**Not touched.** `mr-fetch.ts` is the only other `ghExec` caller; it passes no `timeoutMs` and keeps its current behaviour. Adding a deadline there is a separate decision (it is used for interactive diff/view calls), so I left it alone.

**Pre-existing failure, not from this PR.** `workflow-pr-providers.test.ts > GitHub pull request lookup > ends the lookup at its deadline when a launcher child keeps the output pipe open` fails on this machine with `ENOENT ... holder.pid`. I reverted both changed source files to `main` and it fails identically, so it is local (the fixture's launcher child does not get its pid file out under this filesystem setup), not a regression.

### Successful `gh` calls (head `352bd026`)

`cross-spawn.sync` reports `error: null` when `gh` exits normally, so the `'code' in error` check in `hitTimeout` threw `TypeError: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'code' in null` and every successful `gh` command failed. `hitTimeout` now checks `error instanceof Error` first.

- `npx vitest run src/__tests__/cli-path.test.ts`: the new case with `error: null` fails before the fix with that `TypeError` and passes after. The gh-related unit files pass (105 tests).
- `npm run test:e2e -- src/__tests__/e2e/providers-cli-path.test.ts`, which runs the real `gh --version` through `ghExec`: fails on the previous head with the same `TypeError`, passes here (4 passed, 1 skipped).
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`: passed.

items.title: fix(test): retry the session-pull temp cleanup that races git's gc
items.body:
## Summary

`session-sync-pull` cleaned its temp tree with a bare `fs.rmSync(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true })`. That call failed in a CI run, and every other git-tree cleanup in this repository already guards against exactly this failure.

```
FAIL src/__tests__/session-sync-pull.test.ts > SyncManager.gitPull
     > finishes a merge an earlier pull left stopped on the index
Error: ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty,
  rmdir '/tmp/teamai-test-tmp-F9XRIJ/teamai-session-pull-JQsoY4/b/.git/objects/pack'
```

The test body passed in **153 ms**; the error came from the `afterEach` hook, which vitest reports under the test's name — so it reads like a failed assertion for a merge that actually worked.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (or a fix that changes existing behavior)
- [ ] Documentation only
- [ ] Refactor / internal cleanup

Tests-only, per AGENTS.md: no real-CLI record needed.

## Test Plan

The diff is one `fs.rmSync` call and the comment above it, in `src/__tests__/session-sync-pull.test.ts`:

```diff
-  fs.rmSync(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
+  // A commit or push can leave a detached `git gc --auto` writing objects/pack
+  // after the test returns, so a single rmdir races it (ENOTEMPTY).
+  fs.rmSync(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 100 });
```

- [x] `node --check --experimental-strip-types src/__tests__/session-sync-pull.test.ts` — parses clean
- [x] Byte-level check that nothing else moved: 21378 → 21559 bytes, CR=0, LF 510 → 512, trailing newline kept
- [ ] `npx vitest run` — full suite left to CI (this file is included in all six `Lint & Test` jobs)

## Notes for Reviewers

**This is not a new fix, it is the missing instance of an existing one.** `git-kind-learnings.test.ts` already states the mechanism in a comment:

> A push into the bare origin can leave a detached `git gc --auto` writing to `objects/pack` after the test returns, so a single rmdir races it (ENOTEMPTY).

It passes `maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 100`. Three unit-test files already do the same on their temp tree — `git-kind-learnings`, `learnings-import-remnants`, `reports-reader-lock` — and three of the four e2e files do too (`deleted-worktree-scope-810`, `instruction-targets`, `slash-skill-paths`). This file still removed a tree holding a clone and a bare origin on a single attempt.

**Why I believe it is a timing race and not a broken assertion.** The same commit produced six `Lint & Test` jobs and five passed: Node 20/22/24 on macOS, Node 22/24 on ubuntu. Two of those are ubuntu and run the same file on a newer Node. A logic error would not be that selective.

**What I am not claiming.** I did not identify which detached git process was writing in that particular run — the failing path is `b/.git/objects/pack` while the comment above names a push into the bare origin, and this fixture both commits into `b` (`archive()`) and pushes from it. So this PR does not assert a new root cause; it applies the retry this repository already relies on to the one cleanup that lacked it, and cites the observed failure as the reason.

**Scope.** I deliberately left `helpers/isolate-home.ts` alone. Its `afterAll` also calls a bare `fs.rmSync`, but it removes the outer test directory after every per-test `afterEach` has already emptied it, and the failure above is attributed to the per-test hook. Changing a setup file shared by 555 test files is a different decision from this one.

items.title: fix(ci): retarget label docs at triage.yml and guard that applied labels are declared

labels.name: area:ci
labels.description: GitHub Actions, CI config, repo tooling

labels.name: risk:high
labels.description: High risk: backend API, agents, sandbox, auth, deps, CI

items.body:
### Why

`.github/labels.yml` still describes the auto-labeling setup as three workflows that no longer exist:

- the header says labels are used by `.github/workflows/pr-labeler.yml`, `pr-triage.yml` and `issue-triage.yml`;
- the `area`, `size` and `risk` section headers say `see .github/labeler.yml` / `see pr-triage.yml`.

All four files were removed when `triage.yml` replaced them — that workflow's own header records the swap ("Replaces the former pr-labeler / pr-triage / issue-triage workflows (and drops `actions/labeler`)") — but `labels.yml` was not updated along with it, so every pointer there is a 404.

The same pair had an unguarded failure mode. `triage.yml` applies labels by name at runtime, and GitHub rejects an `addLabels` call with **422** when any requested label does not exist — the whole batch is dropped, so the PR ends up with no labels at all and nothing reports a problem. `labels.yml` states that "every label referenced by a workflow MUST be declared here"; nothing enforced it.

### What changed

- **`.github/labels.yml`** — retarget the header and the three section comments at `.github/workflows/triage.yml`. Comment box widths are unchanged, so the diff is six lines of prose.
- **`scripts/check_label_declarations.py`** (new) — extracts the label literals `triage.yml` can apply and fails when one is missing from `labels.yml`. Standard library only, so the check needs no install step.
- **`.github/workflows/lint-check.yml`** — new `label-declarations` job running that script on every PR.

The check guards itself: an extraction change that matches no labels fails instead of passing silently, and a parse of fewer than 20 declarations from `labels.yml` fails too.

### Verification

Run on this branch:

```text
$ python scripts/check_label_declarations.py
OK -- 22 labels applied by triage.yml are all declared.
```

Mutation check — deleting one declaration makes it fail on exactly that label:

```text
$ python scripts/check_label_declarations.py     # after removing "- name: needs-triage"
1 label(s) applied by triage.yml are not declared in labels.yml:
  - needs-triage
$ echo $?
1
```

Restoring the file returns `rc=0`. `yaml.safe_load` parses all three touched files, and `lint-check.yml` jobs are `agent-guidance`, `label-declarations`, `lint-backend`, `lint-frontend`.

No backend code is touched, so the backend suite is unaffected; the new job needs only the checkout and the stock Python 3.12 that the neighbouring `agent-guidance` job already uses.

items.title: fix: validate inputs_from_state when a tool takes no input

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium priority, add to the next sprint if no P1 available

items.body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #12811

### Proposed Changes:

`Tool.__post_init__` validated `inputs_from_state` against the tool's parameters behind a truthiness guard:

```python
if valid_inputs and param_name not in valid_inputs:
```

Because of the `valid_inputs and` conjunct, "this tool has no input parameters" was indistinguishable from "the parameters could not be determined". For a tool whose valid-parameter set is legitimately empty -- a zero-argument function, a zero-argument `async_function`, or a `ComponentTool` wrapping a component without input sockets -- every mapping target is by definition a typo, yet construction succeeded silently. The mistake then resurfaced much later, inside the agent loop, as a `ToolInvocationError` (`... no_param_tool() got an unexpected keyword argument 'city'`) that never mentions `inputs_from_state`.

This PR removes that conjunct, so the check becomes `if param_name not in valid_inputs:`. An empty set is now validated exactly as strictly as a non-empty one, and the error reads `... Valid parameters are: set().`

Why an empty set is safe to validate against:

- `_get_valid_inputs()` is typed `-> set[str]` and always returns a set -- the union of the callable's signature parameters and the `properties` declared in `parameters`. A tool with no parameters has *resolved* that set and found it empty; that is knowledge, not missing information.
- The sibling `_get_valid_outputs()` is typed `-> set[str] | None` precisely because function-based tools genuinely have no output schema, and its caller tests the sentinel with `is not None` rather than by truthiness. Outputs already distinguish "none" from "unknown"; inputs conflated the two.
- I grepped the codebase: every other use of `inputs_from_state` (`ComponentTool`, `AgentTool`, `PipelineTool`, `create_tool_from_function`) only forwards the mapping into `Tool.__init__`. Nothing relies on the empty-set skip.

The docstring of `_get_valid_inputs()` now states this contract explicitly, so the asymmetry with `_get_valid_outputs()` is documented rather than implicit.

### How did you test it?

Three new tests, one per affected construction path, plus one guard test that the fix is not over-broad. I first reproduced the bug on `main` and then confirmed the fix, with the source change as the only variable.

| test | on `main` (guard restored) | with this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_tool.py::TestTool::test_inputs_from_state_validation_with_no_valid_parameters` | **fail** (`DID NOT RAISE ValueError`) | pass |
| `test_tool.py::TestTool::test_inputs_from_state_validation_with_no_valid_parameters_async_tool` | **fail** (`DID NOT RAISE ValueError`) | pass |
| `test_component_tool.py::TestComponentTool::test_from_component_with_inputs_from_state_and_no_input_sockets` | **fail** (`DID NOT RAISE ValueError`) | pass |
| `test_tool.py::TestTool::test_inputs_from_state_validation_with_empty_mapping_stays_valid` | pass | pass |

In the `ComponentTool` test I assert `tool.parameters == {"type": "object", "properties": {}}` first, as an in-file control that the empty valid set really comes from a component that declares no input sockets rather than from a schema that was not resolved.

Suites run locally (Windows, Python 3.12, `uv` venv):

- `test/tools` -- 296 passed, 14 skipped (292 passed before this PR's four new tests)
- full `test/` with `-m "not integration"` -- 6716 passed, 63 failed; all 63 failures are missing optional dependencies (`torch`, `mdit_plain`, `nltk`, `sentence_transformers`, `oxmsg`) and are unrelated to this change
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the three touched files -- clean

### Notes for the reviewer

The error-message format is intentionally unchanged (`... Valid parameters are: set().`); only the condition that reaches it changed. A friendlier message for the no-parameter case would be a separate, more invasive change, so I kept the diff minimal here -- happy to adjust if you would prefer a different wording.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read the contributors guidelines and code of conduct.
- [x] I have added unit tests and documented the behaviour.
- [x] I have added a release note file.
- [x] I've used a conventional commit type for my PR title (`fix:`).
- [x] I have run the relevant checks locally (ruff, full unit suite).

I used an AI assistant while preparing this change. I have reviewed the diff line by line, reproduced the bug on `main`, verified the fix and the new tests locally, and I take responsibility for the contribution.

items.title: fix(cli): report an async command error as one line, not a stack trace
items.body:
## Summary

The entry boundary reported only `NotInitializedError` as one line. Any other error an async action threw escaped as an unhandled rejection, so Node printed it under a `cli.js:NNNN` header with the whole stack (`teamai session list` outside an initialized project, for example). The boundary now reports whatever a command action throws as one line on stderr and exits 1, and keeps the stack for `--verbose` and `~/.teamai/debug.log`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Test Plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes on the touched files (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- [x] `npx vitest run` passes on every entry test this touches; the full local suite is left to CI (it takes over 15 minutes on this host)
- [x] Added/updated tests for the change
- [x] Real CLI, after `npm run build`, in a cold `$HOME` (see the record below)

### Real CLI

Before (main `d60e68f5`, built the same way), `teamai session list` in an empty cwd:

```
file:///.../dist/cli.js:112960
    throw new Error(
          ^

Error: No teamai project config found. Run `teamai init` or pass --repo-root. Session sync will not use the current working directory.
    at resolveRepoRoot (file:///.../dist/cli.js:112960:11)
    at async _Command.<anonymous> (file:///.../dist/cli.js:113708:22)
    at async _Command.parseAsync (file:///.../dist/cli.js:1902:9)
[exit=1]
```

After:

```
$ teamai session list
stdout: (empty)
stderr: x No teamai project config found. Run `teamai init` or pass --repo-root. Session sync will not use the current working directory.
[exit=1]

$ teamai -v session list
stdout:   [debug] Error: No teamai project config found. ...
            at resolveRepoRoot (...)
stderr: x No teamai project config found. ...
[exit=1]
```

`~/.teamai/debug.log` carries both the `[ERROR]` line and the `[DEBUG]` stack in either mode.

Unchanged: `status`, `env list`, `members list`, `tags list` still print one line and exit 1; `--version` still exits 0.

The new `src/__tests__/e2e/cli-error-exit.test.ts` fails on the build from `main` (2 failed: the stack is in stderr, and `--verbose` prints nothing) and passes on this one.

### Suite note

The entry tests (`index-not-initialized`, `index-migration-trigger`, `index-codebase-help`, `index-import-help`, `cli-path`, `session-cmd`) run as one batch. One of them fails on this Windows host, and it fails the same way with this change reverted:

```
session-cmd.test.ts > session migrate --json > names a Claude Code session whose first lines do not parse unreadable, not not_found
```

The test drives a `--cwd /run/dir` fixture whose POSIX path does not resolve here, so it is not from this PR. The full suite is left to CI.

## Related Issues

Fixes #1270

## Notes for Reviewers

- **The stack goes to stdout under `--verbose`.** That is where `log.debug` already writes (`writeInfoLine`), and `log.debug` also appends to `~/.teamai/debug.log` on every run, so support keeps the trace without a flag. I did not special-case a second destination for it.
- **`reportNotInitialized` stays as it is.** `status`, `list` and `push` still report inside their own action; the boundary is what covers the commands that never wrapped themselves, such as `session list`.
- **Two existing help tests changed.** `index-codebase-help.test.ts` and `index-import-help.test.ts` mock `process.exit` to throw and asserted that the entry *rejects* with it (`rejects.toThrow('process.exit(0)')`). A boundary that reports every error now reports that throw instead, so they await the import and reset `process.exitCode`. The help text they check is already on stdout by then, and in production `--help` / `--version` never reach the boundary: commander calls the real `process.exit`.
- **`index-not-initialized.test.ts` gained four cases** for `reportCommandError` itself: message and exit code without rejecting, the stack reaching `log.debug`, an empty message falling back to the error name, and a thrown non-`Error` value with no invented stack.
- **Seen but left alone:** `teamai digest` prints `Failed to generate digest: teamai is not initialized...` and exits **0**, so a script cannot tell it failed. Different cause, so I did not fold it in here.

items.title: fix(session): honor Cursor CLI's two recorded tool roots
items.body:
## Summary

`teamai init` records a relocated tool root so that every later run targets the directory the tool actually reads. Cursor CLI was not in `RELOCATABLE_TOOLS`, so a member with `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` / `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` set got teamai listing `~/.cursor/projects` and writing the co-author setting to `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`.

Cursor CLI moves **two** directories, and neither of them is the root its `toolPaths` entry hangs off.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## What Cursor CLI reads

Read off the cursor-agent **2026.09.28** bundle, the two directories the issue asks about:

| Root | Variable | Fallback | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| config | `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cursor`, then `~/.cursor` | `cli-config.json`, `permissions.json`, `chats/`, `acp-sessions/` |
| data | `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` (also `--data-dir`) | `~/.cursor` | `projects/` — the transcripts |

The user `mcp.json`, `rules/` and `commands/` stay in `~/.cursor` whatever the variables say.

## Why the two roots are not recorded as `cursor`

`applyToolRoots` re-roots the `toolPaths` entry of every key it finds in `toolRoots`, so a key named `cursor` would move `toolPaths.cursor` — the user `mcp.json`, `rules/` and `commands/` that have to stay put. The roots are therefore recorded as **`cursor-data`** and **`cursor-config`**: `RELOCATABLE_TOOLS` holds roots, not tool ids, and its doc block now says so. `src/__tests__/cursor-tool-roots.test.ts` pins that `scopedToolPaths` leaves `cursor` where it is.

## What follows the record now

- **Transcripts.** `getCursorProjectsDir(toolRoots)` resolves `<data root>/projects`. The `cursor` entry of `ADAPTER_REGISTRY` forwards `toolRoots`, and `CursorAdapter` takes the resolved store in its constructor instead of closing over the default — the shape `#1135` gave `ClaudeCodeAdapter` and `CodexAdapter`.
- **`cli-config.json`.** New `cursorConfigDir()` in `types.ts`; `coauthor-reconcile.ts` writes there instead of a bare `path.join(userHome, '.cursor', ...)`. This is the one place `toolRoots` cannot express the answer — `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` names a parent directory, and `~/.config` itself is refused as a root — so the fallback is read where the write happens.
- **The IDE half (item 3).** Neither CLI variable applies to the Cursor IDE: it resolves its user-data dir the way VS Code does (`VSCODE_PORTABLE` → `VSCODE_APPDATA` → `--user-data-dir`, and on Linux `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `~/.config`, joined with `Cursor`). `session-flow/cursor-store.ts` was the one place that hard-coded `~/.config/Cursor`; it now honors `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, as `ide-history.ts` already does for the same IDE.

## Test Plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- [x] Added/updated tests for the change
- [ ] `npx vitest run` — I could not run the full suite here; see "Regression check" for what I ran instead

**New and updated tests**

- `src/__tests__/cursor-tool-roots.test.ts` (new, 11 cases) — the recorded keys, the transcript store (list, read and write under the recorded root, `~/.cursor` left alone), the config root through the real `reconcileCoAuthorForConfig`, and the IDE store root (including a blank `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). **53 passed** together with the updated `tool-roots.test.ts`. Its cleanup hook declares `60_000`: removing the fixture is I/O bound, and this box's temp volume is slow enough to miss the 15s default — the repo gives 84 other hooks an explicit budget for the same reason.
- `src/__tests__/e2e/cursor-tool-roots-1138.test.ts` (new, 3 cases) — the real CLI end to end. **3 passed** (below).
- `src/__tests__/tool-roots.test.ts` — the refusal message now names the four supported keys.
- `src/__tests__/coauthor-reconcile.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/cursor-user-images.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/agent-session-copy.test.ts` — pin `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` so the fixtures and the code agree whatever the runner exports. No assertion changed; see "Fixes after the first CI run".

**Regression check.** I ran the same selection on the change and on the unmodified tree (same tarball), because on this Windows box a failure cannot be attributed without that:

```
$ npx vitest run --pool=threads src/__tests__/agent-session-platform.test.ts \
    src/__tests__/agent-session-list.test.ts src/__tests__/agent-session-tool-roots.test.ts \
    src/__tests__/session-cmd.test.ts src/__tests__/doctor.test.ts \
    src/__tests__/skip-uninstalled-tools.test.ts src/__tests__/usage-tracking.test.ts

```

### 2) CURSOR_DATA_DIR=$HOME/cursordata CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/cursorconfig teamai init .
ℹ Recorded CURSOR_DATA_DIR as the Cursor transcripts root: <HOME>/cursordata

```

**The E2E file, run the way `AGENTS.md` says to:**

```
$ npm run test:e2e -- src/__tests__/e2e/cursor-tool-roots-1138.test.ts
ESM ⚡️ Build success in 1067ms
