
The three cases declare `120_000`, following the ~237 cases in this suite that do. That is not decoration: on this machine a fixture that runs `teamai init` costs ~30s per call, so the two-init case lands at ~62-70s and misses the 60s default. The same machine, same default budget, on the **unmodified** `src/__tests__/e2e/init-self-agent-filter.test.ts`: 2 of its 6 cases fail on that timeout (`re-running init…` 62.1s, `any other command still self-heals…` 64.2s) and pass once raised. So the timeout is the machine, not the change.

## Fixes after the first CI run

The first push came back `Lint & Test` **failed on ubuntu-latest, passed on macos-latest** (all three Node versions each way). Two causes, both in this change:

1. **Three existing test files inherited `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.** `coauthor-reconcile.test.ts`, `cursor-user-images.test.ts` and `agent-session-copy.test.ts` build their expectations under `~/.cursor` / `~/.config/Cursor` but never pin the variable — unlike the rest of the suite, where `agent-session-list.test.ts:79` pins it and every E2E file does. With the new code reading that variable, they resolved a different directory than the fixture wrote and read back `undefined`. Each now pins it the way the rest of the repo does. **No assertion changed**; the variable-set path is covered by the new file instead.

   Evidence: on this Windows box, exporting `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and re-running reproduces the ubuntu set — `coauthor-reconcile.test.ts` 3 failed and `cursor-user-images.test.ts` 1 failed, with the same case names and messages as the annotations. Unset, both pass. The four `agent-session-copy.test.ts` cases are `skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')`, so they cannot appear here at all; the annotations are the evidence for those. macOS never sets the variable — that is why it stayed green.

2. **A blank `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` was read as set.** `getCursorStateRoot()` used `??`, which keeps `''`, so `path.join('', 'Cursor')` returned the *relative* path `Cursor` — the working directory. It is `?.trim() ||` now, matching `switch.ts` and the `$XDG_DATA_HOME` read the OpenCode adapter already does (`opencode.ts:307`) — both treat a blank variable as unset — and `cursor-tool-roots.test.ts` pins the blank case. (`ide-history.ts:139` has the same `??` shape for a different IDE; out of scope here, and I left it alone rather than widen the diff.)

Cause 1 is what CI showed; cause 2 is the P2 finding the bot review filed on the PR.

**The `E2E (fork-safe, no credentials)` check is red on every fork PR here.** It fails on #1062 (damenjs) exactly as it does on this one — a fork PR runs that variant and skips the other. Its annotations on this PR are `workflow-subworkflow` / `workflow-inline` (`record: 'pending'`), which is workflow code this change does not touch; #1161 and #1154 have since changed that code on `main`, so re-running may clear it.

## Related Issues

Addresses items 1 and 3 of #1138. Item 2 is #1142's and item 4 is untouched.

## Notes for Reviewers

- **Version checked**, as the issue asks: cursor-agent **2026.09.28** for the two variables and their fallbacks, **Cursor 3.16.29** for the IDE. If a newer build resolves differently, only two places move: `RELOCATABLE_TOOLS` (`cursor-data`, `cursor-config`) and `cursorConfigDir()`.
- **`doctor` does not cover the two new keys.** `buildToolRootChecks` compares where teamai would write a tool's `toolPaths` against where that tool reads them; these two roots have no `toolPaths` entry — that is the point — so the check skips them, and a stale record of either root goes unreported. Covering it needs a check that is not `toolPaths`-shaped; I left it out rather than widen this PR, and because that comment block sits inside `#1119`'s insertion point.
- **`releasePreviousToolRoots` skips them too**, since `isAgentExcluded` reads a `cursor-data` key as an agent that is not enabled. Nothing is lost: neither root holds hooks or the managed MCP files, which is what that pass cleans up.
- **Rebased onto `c57da5af`.** `#1148` (`src/types.ts`, +2 lines) and `#1062` (`src/init.ts`, new import and push path) merged while this was open. The patch applied to both with a 2-line offset only, and `tsc` / `lint` pass on the rebased tree. Remaining open overlap is `src/types.ts` (#1040, #1119, #1143). `#1142` ("honor Muse XDG data home", by @SIBTAIN-ASAD) touches only `dashboard-collector.ts` and its tests — a different XDG consumer, no overlap. `#1157` (Cursor skill-usage hook matcher) touches hooks, not the session store.

items.title: feat(hooks): config switch for the SessionStart MR hint
items.body:
## What this does

Adds the config switch #1103 asks for: a team can turn the SessionStart MR hint
off without touching `contributeHint`, and a member can turn it off on one
machine without exporting an env var in every shell that starts an agent.

Precedence mirrors `isContributeHintEnabled` exactly:

```
TEAMAI_MR_HINT_DISABLED=1  >  mrHintEnabled (~/.teamai/config.yaml)  >  sharing.mrHint.enabled (teamai.yaml)  >  true
```

## Both entry points honor it, from one resolution

`computeMrHintOutput` has two callers, and the switch is resolved in the one path
they share, so the two cannot disagree about it.

Per @SaulMoro's note, the legacy `teamai mr-hint` path already resolved its scope
to get `language` — it just threw the config away. `mrHint()` now resolves the
scope once and feeds both the language and the switch from that same config,
in place of `loadTeamAgentLanguageForHook` (which `todowrite-hint` still uses):

- the SessionStart hook passes the scope it already received;
- the legacy `teamai mr-hint` command resolves it once, for both values.

## Kept separate from `contributeHint` (#988)

`isMrHintEnabled` is its own resolver rather than a reuse of
`contributeHintAllowed`: the latter also goes quiet when recall is off, and #988
settled that the MR hint does not follow recall — #1057 tried to gate it on that
switch and was closed, #1060 documented the split. Neither switch can move the
other.

## Tests

- **`mr-hint-toggle.test.ts` (new)** — the full precedence chain; that a scope's
  `mrHint` never reads `contributeHint`; that both new schema keys parse while
  existing configs stay valid; and that a scope with the switch off returns
  before the hint probes the repo. The last three count the hint's own
  `git remote get-url origin` call — 0 when the switch is off, 1 when it is on —
  so the "off" cases cannot pass by accident.
- **`hook-handlers.test.ts`** — the two #1014 language tests now assert the
  resolved scope is passed alongside the language.

`tsc --noEmit` is clean. Focused run of the six affected suites: **193 tests,
192 passed, 1 failed**. The one failure is pre-existing and unrelated:
`contribute-check handler withholds the reminder when the payload cwd exists but
cannot be checked` relies on `statSync` returning `ENOTDIR` for a path through a
file. On Windows it returns `ENOENT` instead, and the same test fails on
`bcdb39c` with no changes applied. CI runs ubuntu/macos only, where it is green.

## Real-CLI verification

Built with `npm run build` and exercised the standalone entry point, flipping
only `sharing.mrHint.enabled` in `teamai.yaml` between runs. Same build output,
same command (`teamai mr-hint --stdin --tool claude`), same scope, same git
remote; each run on a cold `$HOME` so the hint cache cannot mask the result:

| `sharing.mrHint.enabled` | stdout |
|---|---|
| `false`, two separate runs | **empty** (0 B) |
| `true`, two separate runs | **2141 B** SessionStart hint, both byte-identical |

The `true` run lists ten real merged MRs from the scope's remote:

```
[teamai:mr-hint] 发现 10 个近期已合入但尚未提炼的 MR。
  teamai import --from-mr https://github.com/Tencent/teamai-cli/pull/1114
  … (#1098)
```

The `false` runs turn the hint off **before any repo probe**: with `GIT_TRACE`
pointed at a file, they make zero `git remote get-url origin` calls, while the
`true` runs make exactly one. Flipping the switch back and forth in separate
cold `$HOME`s reproduces both sides exactly. A full provider × agent matrix is
not reproduced here, per the review rules — one representative run is.

Fixes #1103

items.title: fix(doctor): check that the zcode SessionStart hook actually answers
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #1050. `doctor`'s ZCode delivery becomes two checks instead of one. #1047 renamed the existing check to say what it actually verifies — registration — and deliberately left the gap open: the entry can be present, `hooks.enabled` can be `true`, and the hook can still deliver nothing. That is exactly what happened in #1030.

The new check runs the entry **the config actually registers**, with its dispatch tail swapped for a stub, and requires the reply to come back. Registration keeps answering the other question, so a broken entry reports once as "not registered" and once as "cannot answer" — never as a false green.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation only
- [ ] Refactor / internal cleanup

## What it does

`src/doctor-delivery.ts`:

- `sessionStartDispatchEntries` returns the `SessionStart` entries that dispatch a teamai session-start, as `{ command, args }` pairs; `sessionStartDispatches` becomes a thin wrapper over it, so the registration check and the probe share one filter.
- `zcodeEntryCarriesItsReply` spawns that command with its **last argument** replaced:
  - `node -e "process.stdin.pipe(process.stdout)"`, fed a known payload — the payload must come back in stdout;
  - `node -e "process.exit(7)"` — the status must survive the hop.
- The check is added only when the entry is registered **and** `hooks.enabled === true`; otherwise the existing check already fails and names the reason, so nothing is reported twice.
- Bounded (10 s per probe), read-only, and it never runs the real dispatch — a SessionStart dispatch carries a network pull (`toZcodeEntry`).

## Why the tail is swapped instead of running the hook live

Running the registered command as-is would hit the team host on every `doctor`, and `hooks inject`/`pull`/`init` must stay cheap. Replacing only the tail keeps the part #1030 actually broke under test — on Windows the entry's own `args[0]` is the Node launcher, which is exactly where the stdout was dropped — and drops the network. Building these checks already only happens in the `doctor` stage (`doctor.ts:578`), so no pull pays for the spawn.

## Test Plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes (oxlint --type-aware, 883 files, 0 warnings / 0 errors)
- [x] `npx vitest run --pool=threads src/__tests__/project-hook-rules.test.ts src/__tests__/zcode.test.ts src/__tests__/doctor-delivery.test.ts src/__tests__/builtin-hooks.test.ts` — 4 files, 108 tests pass
- [x] Red/green: with `src/doctor-delivery.ts` reverted to `main`, 3 of the 4 new tests fail (the fourth asserts the check's *absence*, which is true on both revisions); with the change, all 43 tests in the file pass
- [x] Real-CLI record below

## Real-CLI record

`npm run build`, then a scratch HOME and a git project scope:

```
$ teamai hooks inject
✔ Updated teamai hooks in ...\home\.zcode\cli\config.json

$ teamai doctor --json
PASS  The teamai SessionStart hook is registered and enabled for zcode
PASS  The teamai SessionStart hook for zcode returns its reply to the session

# launcher replaced with the pre-fix one (spawnSync(..., { stdio: 'ignore' }))
$ teamai doctor --json
PASS  The teamai SessionStart hook is registered and enabled for zcode
FAIL  The teamai SessionStart hook for zcode returns its reply to the session
      fix: ...\home\.zcode\cli\config.json registers the teamai SessionStart hook and turns hooks on,
      but running that entry's own command handed back nothing where the dispatch should have answered
      (or lost its exit status), so a session would start with none of the team rules while registration
      still looks healthy (#1030). On Windows the entry goes through the Node launcher beside this file.
      Run `teamai hooks inject` to rewrite it. ...
```

The registration check stays green in the second run on purpose: that pair is the #1030 shape, and it is what the new check exists to break.

## Notes for Reviewers

- **The probe compares a substring, not the whole stdout.** On POSIX the entry runs its tail through `bash -lc`, and a login profile that prints lands in front of the reply. The failure to catch is the reply going missing, not extra bytes around it.
- **On POSIX this is a weaker check than on Windows, and knowingly so.** The POSIX entry is `bash -lc <dispatch>`, with no launcher hop; replacing the tail leaves `bash -lc` plus the stub, so it only proves the shell can run the payload. #1030 was Windows-only for the same reason — the launcher exists only there. I gated nothing on the platform: the check is meaningful where the launcher is, and harmless where it is not.
- **`node` is taken from the entry's own `command`**, i.e. from PATH. A machine where ZCode can run the hook but `doctor` cannot resolve `node` gets a failure rather than a skip; the fix text names that case.
- Both stubs are teamai's own and touch nothing but the three stdio handles.

items.title: 精选时间线增加「只看未读」筛选
items.body:
## 解决什么问题

精选时间线（`/` 及其类别、tag 视图）新增一个「只看未读」开关，对应 #185。反复回来查看精选时，后续入选的报道会被插入较早的时间线位置、夹在已读的灰色卡片之间，只看列表顶部容易漏掉；这个开关把本机已读的卡片收起来，只留没打开过的。

行为按 #185 里确认过的范围实现：

- 默认关闭；开启后只隐藏本机已读的精选，精选判定、排序、阅读组和收藏都不变。
- 已读仍是浏览器本地那份记录（`apps/web/app/lib/local-state.ts` 的 `useReadSet()`），不上传服务端，不新增账户或同步。
- 阅读组按「组内是否还有未读的精选报道」判断：代表文章已读、但组里其他精选报道没读过时卡片保留；普通（非精选）报道不参与这个判断。
- 当前已加载的卡片全部读过时自动继续取下一页，直到出现未读内容；边界与列表本身一致 —— 到自动批次上限（`AUTO_BATCHES`）后交回「加载更多」按钮，加载失败保留原有的重试入口。
- 筛选开启时，日头「N 条」按当前可见卡片数显示。后端的 `dayCounts` 是整天的全量计数、不感知本机已读，直接沿用会和可见条数自相矛盾。

实现分两处：

- `packages/contracts/src/site.ts` 的 `GroupInfo` 增加可选的 `memberIds: string[]`；`packages/backend/src/publication/timeline.ts` 在构造阅读组时用**已有的** `candidates`（该事实下当前筛选内的精选成员，本来就要查出来挑代表）填进去，没有新增查询。文章页的 `GroupInfo`（`detail.ts`）不需要这个字段，所以做成可选。
- `apps/web/app/features/feed/Timeline.tsx` 加筛选状态（存在列表快照里，返回时一并恢复）、过滤规则、自动续页和开关；开关复用站内已有的 `ToggleChip`。

## 如何验证

新增 `apps/web/tests/timeline-unread.test.ts`，用真实 web server 加合成 API 覆盖 #185 点名的场景，5 项全部通过：

1. 已加载的两张卡片都已读时，开筛选会自己翻到下一页并显示那篇未读；已读卡片确实不出现。
2. 下一页加载失败时出现「加载失败，点此重试」，重试后成功，且筛选仍是开启状态。
3. 开启筛选 → 打开一篇未读报道 → 返回列表：筛选保留（`aria-pressed=true`），刚打开的报道因已读不再显示，同页另一篇未读报道可见。
4. 阅读组在「代表已读、组内另有未读」时保留；组内全部已读时消失。
5. 全部已读且没有下一页时显示「没有未读的精选内容」，而不是看起来像空列表。

本地（Node 24，`npm ci` 安装，`package-lock.json` 未改动）：

- `npm run typecheck`：通过（六个 `tsc` 项目加 `@aihot/web`）。
- `npm run build -w @aihot/web`：成功。
- `node --test apps/web/tests/timeline-unread.test.ts`：5 项全部通过。
- `npm run test:standalone`：180 项，177 通过、3 失败（`outbound-headers` 的 2 项 `UND_ERR_HEADERS_OVERFLOW`，加 `migration-check` 的 `spawnSync git EBUSY`）。
- `node --test apps/web/tests/*.test.ts`（新增文件之外）：13 条失败行，本机未装 WebKit 等环境原因。
- 上面两组失败都与本改动无关：`git stash` 掉改动、**重建产物**后在未改动状态重跑，失败集合逐条一致（零差异）。
- 本机没有 PostgreSQL，`npm test` 未在本地跑。

## 兼容与使用影响

- 新增的 `GroupInfo.memberIds` 是可选的，只有时间线填；已有响应字段一个都没动，文章页响应形状不变。
- 不涉及数据库、`.env.example`、公开 API 或升级步骤。
- 开关默认关闭，未开启时时间线的展示与之前完全一致；筛选状态只存在本机列表快照里，不写服务端。
- 已读记录沿用现有的 localStorage 格式（`aihot-read-items`），没有新增存储键。

items.title: fix: deliver the ZCode SessionStart hook through a Node launcher
items.body:
## Summary

On Windows the ZCode `SessionStart` hook was registered but never delivered anything: the teamai launcher ran the hook through `wscript.exe` with a `>nul 2>&1`, so the JSON payload `session-start` writes to stdout was thrown away — and the request ZCode piped into stdin was unreadable in the first place. This replaces the generated WSH launcher with a Node launcher that inherits both std handles and hands them to the hook unchanged.

Fixes #1030.

## Root cause — three defects in one launcher

The launcher generated by `reconcileZcodeFormat` was a `.vbs` invoked as `wscript.exe <launcher.vbs> "<tail>"`, and the entry looked like:

```json
{ "type": "process", "command": "wscript.exe", "args": ["<...>/teamai-hook-dispatch.vbs", "<tail>"] }
```

1. **stdout is discarded.** The template ends with

   ```vbs
   sh.Run "cmd /d /s /c """ & WScript.Arguments(0) & " < """ & spool & """ >nul 2>&1""", 0, True
   ```

   The `>nul 2>&1` sends the hook's stdout to the null device. The `team-rules` handler's only output channel is `process.stdout.write(...)` (`src/hook-dispatch-cli.ts:491`), so the project rules could never reach ZCode.

2. **stdin is unreadable — and, when readable, re-encoded.** `WScript.StdIn` / `StdOut` / `StdErr` exist **only under `cscript.exe`**. Under `wscript.exe` they raise; the template's `On Error Resume Next` swallows it and `WScript.StdIn.ReadAll()` yields an empty spool. This codebase already records the second half of the problem: `src/hook-dispatch-cli.ts:139` documents that "the hidden VBS launcher decodes the UTF-8 payload through the ANSI codepage, so a payload containing multi-byte text can break the JSON structure at the first non-ASCII sequence" — which is why `salvageStdinFields()` exists at all. The launcher could therefore corrupt a request as well as lose the reply.

3. **The exit code is dropped.** `WshShell.Run`'s return value is never inspected, so ZCode saw `0` regardless of what the hook decided.

## Why the launcher does not stay on WSH

@SaulMoro's correction in #1030 is right, and it is the reason the fix cannot simply be "switch the host to `cscript.exe`": those three properties are `cscript`-only, so the host has to change — but `cscript` then breaks the payload on the way out.

**Why `cscript.exe` does not work either.** When its stdout is redirected, WSH does not emit UTF-8. From Eric Lippert's *Unicode output and the Windows Script Host* ([Microsoft, archived on MS Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/ericlippert/unicode-output-and-the-windows-script-host)):

> If you are running cscript.exe on an NT-based OS and you've redirected your console output to a file, and you did NOT specify the //U switch then we dump the text as ANSI by calling `WideCharToMultiByte(CP_OEMCP)`. In the same scenario but with the //U switch we dump the text as UTF-16.

So `cscript` offers a choice of **ANSI/OEM** (non-ASCII project rules re-encoded or replaced with substitution characters) or **UTF-16** (not the UTF-8 the pipe contract expects) — never UTF-8. `WScript.StdOut.Write` is unusable for the same reason.

The remaining WSH constructs do not close the gap either: the spool-file trick still has to emit through `WScript.StdOut` (absent under `wscript.exe`), `WshShell.Run` gives no access to the parent's stdout, and `WshShell.Exec` can capture a child's stdout but offers no window-style control.

The only construct that carries stdin and stdout through **byte-for-byte** is a real executable spawned with inherited handles.

## The fix — a Node launcher

`reconcileZcodeFormat` now writes `teamai-hook-dispatch.mjs` beside the config. The entry produced on win32 is literally:

```json
{"type":"process","command":"node",
 "args":["<...>\\.zcode\\cli\\teamai-hook-dispatch.mjs","teamai hook-dispatch session-start --tool zcode"],
 "timeoutMs":180000}
```

which is the `process` shape ZCode's own documentation recommends. The generated launcher (303 bytes, sha1 `1da76738ce174fdd871f2518d686625b16df5ac8`):

```js
// TeamAI hook dispatcher: argv-preserving, invisible, exit-code transparent.
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const tail = process.argv[2];
if (!tail) process.exit(1);

const { status } = spawnSync(tail, { shell: true, stdio: 'inherit', windowsHide: true });
process.exit(status ?? 1);
```

- `stdio: 'inherit'` hands the hook the same handles the launcher received, so the JSON request arrives on stdin and the reply goes back to ZCode's pipe **byte-for-byte** — no code-page conversion, and no spool file. Both defects (1) and (2) die with the same line.
- `windowsHide: true` keeps the intermediate `cmd` from creating a console window.
- The exit code is propagated, so ZCode can still tell `0` (parse stdout) from `2` (blocking) from a recoverable failure.
- The legacy `teamai-hook-dispatch.vbs` is now deleted unconditionally on inject and on `removeAll`, so a stale launcher cannot linger.

## Scope

As agreed with @SaulMoro:

- the launcher fix above;
- `doctor`: the check is a **registration** check, not a delivery check. It is renamed (`Project rules reach zcode through its SessionStart hook` → `The teamai SessionStart hook is registered and enabled for zcode`) and its fix texts now state what is actually verified. **The check logic is unchanged**; a functional delivery check is left to a follow-up.
- `hooks.maxOutputBytes` (default `32768`, covering the whole JSON response) is untouched, and this change never truncates — the inherited stream is passed through as-is.
- The `salvageStdinFields()` fallback stays: it still serves other hosts, and removing it is not this PR's business.

## Changes

8 files, `+131 −86`:

| file | +/− | change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/hooks.ts` | +66 −51 | entry `wscript.exe` → `node`; template rewritten; legacy `.vbs` cleanup; `zcodeLauncherPath` helpers |
| `src/doctor-delivery.ts` | +12 −7 | check renamed, fix wording made truthful |
| `src/__tests__/zcode.test.ts` | +48 −23 | updated assertions + a new case asserting the legacy `.vbs` is deleted on inject *and* on `removeAll` |
| `src/__tests__/project-hook-rules.test.ts` | +1 −1 | renamed check |
| `docs/guide/windows.md` · `zh-CN/windows.md` | +1 −1 each | "`wscript.exe` launcher" → Node launcher |
| `docs/guide/advanced.md` · `zh-CN/advanced.md` | +1 −1 each | the ZCode hook paragraph rewritten; the ANSI-code-page caveat is dropped because it no longer applies |

## Verification

On Windows, on this machine:

- `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `oxlint src/` — 0 warnings, 0 errors (862 files, 96 rules)
- `zcode.test.ts` + `project-hook-rules.test.ts` — **52 passed**
- **End-to-end probe against the launcher this code actually generated.** The launcher file under test is not a hand-written stand-in: it was produced by running `reconcileHooks(configPath, 'zcode')` on a throwaway home and copied straight out of `~/.zcode/cli/` (303 bytes, sha1 `1da76738ce174fdd871f2518d686625b16df5ac8`). The probe spawns it exactly as the entry does (`node <launcher> "<tail>"`) with a real stdin pipe, and the hook stand-in replies with the shape `teamRulesHandler` returns:

  ```
  PASS  exit code 0 reaches the caller  ::  status=0
  PASS  stdout equals the handler reply byte-for-byte  ::  158B vs expected 158B
  PASS  stdin arrives unchanged (non-ASCII included)  ::  echoed 97B of 97B
  PASS  the reply carries non-ASCII text unmangled
  PASS  non-zero exit 2 propagates through the launcher  ::  status=2
  PASS  large multi-byte request (9044B) survives intact  ::  status=0
  PASS  missing tail argument exits 1  ::  status=1
  PASS  generated launcher passes `node --check`  ::  status=0
  ```

  The same launcher was also exercised with the real `hook-dispatch session-start --tool zcode` command (built from this tree) as its tail: the command started and ran through the launcher's inherited handles, confirming the argv/shell path as well as the stdio path.

### Still to confirm at runtime — **Windows + ZCode verification is pending**

I have no ZCode Desktop installation here, so these are **not** proven and need a run on a real Windows + ZCode desktop:

1. the project rules actually reach a **new ZCode session**;
2. non-ASCII project content arrives unchanged through the whole path;
3. **no console window flashes** when the hook fires.

For (1) and (2) the launcher side is proven above; what remains unexercised is ZCode's own spawn and its handling of the returned JSON. (3) is the one genuine regression risk of leaving WSH — `wscript.exe` is a GUI-subsystem binary and never drew a window, whereas `node` is console-subsystem, so whether a window appears depends on the spawn flags ZCode uses. The entry schema exposes no window option, so only a real run can answer it. @SaulMoro has offered to ask @d542Bb (who reported the adjacent #1029 on Windows + ZCode Desktop) to check these three; the result will be recorded here.

items.title: fix(toolRoots): accept roots nested below ~/.config/<name>
items.body:
Closes #1010.

`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` can point several levels below `~/.config`: a per-directory profile manager such as [cloak](https://github.com/juniormartinxo/cloak) puts it at `~/.config/cloak/profiles/work/claude`. `teamai init` refused to record that root, warned, and left the sync on `~/.claude` — so the hooks were written to a settings file the tool never reads, and the session sync silently did nothing.

## Why this is more than relaxing one predicate

My first revision only loosened `isAddressableRootSegment`. That is not enough, and looking at it the way the gate does shows why: **the installed-tool gate does not read the recorded root — it derives one from the path's shape.**

`toolInstallRoot` keys a `.config/...` path on its first two segments, so for the root above it probes `.config/cloak`. That directory can exist for an unrelated reason while the recorded root itself does not, and then the gate calls the tool installed and the write recreates a root the user had deleted — the very thing the gate exists to prevent.

So the two meanings get separated.

## What changed

`toolInstallRoot` keeps answering from the path's shape. `relocateToolPaths` matches against it and `applyToolRoots` re-roots at it, so it must stay independent of any recorded root.

`toolGateRoot` is new, and is what the gate reads:

```ts
export function toolGateRoot(
  tool: string,
  toolPath: string,
  toolRoots?: Record<string, string>,
): string {
  const recorded = toolRoots?.[tool];
  if (recorded) {
    const segment = toolRootSegment(tool, recorded);
    if (segment && (toolPath === segment || toolPath.startsWith(`${segment}/`))) return segment;
  }
  return toolInstallRoot(toolPath);
}
```

The record is used only when `toolPath` really hangs off it — the same `toolPaths` are used unrelocated in project scope, where a HOME-relative member root says nothing — and only after `toolRootSegment` has vetted it (unregistered tool, rejected root: both fall through). **With no recorded root the two functions agree, so every existing setup behaves exactly as before.**

`isAddressableRootSegment` then accepts any depth under `.config/`:

```diff
-  return segments.length === 2 && segments[0] === '.config';
+  return segments[0] === '.config';
```

Roots nested outside `.config` (`~/configs/claude`, `~/.local/share/claude`) stay refused.

Gate call sites now thread the record through: `injectHooksToAllTools`, `reconcileHooksToAllTools`, `hooksRemove`, the two user-scope probes in `pull.ts` and `pre-push-sync.ts`, and `known-agents.ts`'s `seedToolRoots` / `seedHookInstallRoot` — the last two have to agree with the gate, or a self-mode nested root would never get its hooks.

The text that describes the root moves with the code. `docs/guide/reference.md` and its Chinese pair no longer say the check keys on `.config/<name>`; it reads the recorded root. `skill-data/core/references/troubleshooting.md` no longer tells agents a root nested below `~/.config/<name>` cannot be synced. And `toolRootRejection` drops the same stale justification — `.config/` is required so the check can tell the tool's root from an unrelated directory, not because that prefix is what it reads.

## Verified

**Real CLI, single-variable pair** — `teamai hooks inject` with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.config/cloak/profiles/work/claude`. The only thing that varies is whether the recorded root exists on disk:

| scenario | control build (`toolGateRoot` degrades to `toolInstallRoot`) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| **X** — only `.config/cloak` exists | `✔ Updated teamai hooks in …\.config\cloak\profiles\work\claude\settings.json`, and the whole stale path is created | `✔ Hooks injected into all AI tool settings`; under `.config` the tree stays `.config`, `.config/cloak` — **nothing written** |
| **Y** — the recorded root exists | writes into it | writes into it |

The control build reproduces the failure mode this PR is about; this branch stops it while still delivering to a root that is really there.

**Unit tests** — `src/__tests__/tool-roots.test.ts`, 42 passed, including six cases for `toolGateRoot` (reads the record; agrees with the path shape whenever the two can agree; ignores a record the path does not hang off; ignores a record the tool may not relocate; still skips a missing two-segment root) and a single-variable pair on `isToolInstalledForConfig`.

Mutation-checked: dropping the record branch inside `toolGateRoot` turns exactly the four intended cases red (4 failed / 38 passed) and leaves the controls green.

`tsc --noEmit` and `oxlint` are clean.

## Regression check

The branch is rebased onto `2cbf5560`: the tree is that commit plus exactly these thirteen files. #1002 (#904) touched the same gate function — the tail of `isToolInstalledForConfig` in `src/resources/base.ts` — so the resolution keeps its `EDITION_HOME_ROOTS` branch first and threads `toolGateRoot` into the probe call after it; `src/types.ts` keeps #1002's Trae schema and `MCP_MANIFEST_KEY_ALIAS` alongside `toolGateRoot`.

Against a pristine `2cbf5560` checkout, the eight gate-related test files produce **identical failure sets** — `tool-roots`, `doctor`, `trae`, `qoder-cn`, `hooks`, `hooks-cmd`, `init`, `instruction-targets`; every failure is already on the base (Windows path shapes, `EBUSY` under the runner, the three `filterAgents` cases).

Against the original base `b69f8889` the affected test files behave the same: eleven identical failure sets, and `pull-agent-models` produces one *fewer* failure than the base (11 vs 12) — only `Test timed out in 15000ms` / `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, rmdir …\Temp\…`, no assertion on either revision.

## Not touched

`applyToolRoots` / `relocateToolPaths` / `resolveToolRootDir` are string operations and were already depth-agnostic. The `.config/<name>` keying in `toolInstallRoot` is deliberately unchanged. `toolRoots` for tools other than `claude` / `codex` is unchanged.

items.title: 删掉告警配置里没被读取的 modelStops 字段
items.body:
## 解决什么问题

`site/site.ts` 的 `ALERTS` 里有一个 `modelStops` 字段（`Record<string, string>`，默认空对象），注释说它用于“某家模型服务拒绝服务或额度用完时，告警里说哪些步骤停了”。这个字段从声明起就没有被任何代码读取。

告警里“哪些步骤停了”这句实际来自 `packages/backend/src/operations/alerts.ts`：`providerStops()`（第 220 行）先查硬编码的 `PROVIDERS` 表（第 209 行），没有 `stops` 的模型服务再交给同文件的局部函数 `modelStops(service)`（第 204 行）按 `stepsOnService()` 现算。全程不读 `site.ts`。

全仓库检索 `modelStops` 只有两处命中，就是 `alerts.ts` 里那个同名局部函数的定义和调用点；`site.ts` 的字段一个读取点都没有。`ALERTS` 的实际消费点只有三处：`alerts.ts:29` 读 `quietMinutes`、`alerts.ts:52` 读 `usualFlow`、`operations/watch.ts:42` 读 `workerLogs` —— 删除后剩下的三个字段正好与之对应。

所以站长配了这个字段不会有任何效果。删掉它不改变任何运行时行为。

说明一下为什么现有检查没查到它：`tests/architecture.test.ts` 第 108 行那条 “nothing kept that nothing uses” 规则的两处范围（第 112 行的 `PRODUCTION`、第 119 行 DB 列检查用的目录）都不包含 `site/`，所以“site 里声明、代码从不读”的字段不在它的检查面内。这次只按最小改动处理这个字段本身，没有顺带扩大那条规则的覆盖范围 —— 那是另一个决定，不该混在这个 PR 里。

## 如何验证

改动本身：

- `git diff`：`site/site.ts` 删 2 行（1 行注释 + 1 行字段），无其他改动。
- 改动后全仓库检索 `modelStops`：只剩 `alerts.ts` 里那个同名局部函数的定义和调用点，`site.ts` 已无该字段。
- `ALERTS` 的消费点仍是三处，与删除后剩下的三个字段（`quietMinutes`、`usualFlow`、`workerLogs`）一一对应。

本地能跑的部分（Node 24，`npm ci` 安装，未改动 `package-lock.json`）：

- `npm run typecheck`：通过。六个 `tsc` 项目（`contracts`、`backend`、`apps/api`、`apps/worker`、`tests`、`modules`）加 `@aihot/web` 的 `react-router typegen && tsc -p .` 全部无错。
- `npm run build -w @aihot/web`：构建成功。
- `npm run test:standalone`：181 项，179 通过、2 失败。失败的两项在 `tests/outbound-headers.standalone.test.ts`，报 `UND_ERR_HEADERS_OVERFLOW`。
- `node --test apps/web/tests/*.test.ts`：50 项，32 通过、18 失败；本机未安装 Playwright 浏览器。
- 上面两组失败都与本改动无关：把改动 `git stash` 掉、在同一分支的未改动状态重跑，失败集合完全一致（分别是同样的 2 项和同样的 18 项，逐条零差异）。
- 本机没有 PostgreSQL 实例，`npm test` 没在本地跑。

本仓库 CI：`check` 与 `docker` 两个 workflow 在这个提交上都是成功。`check` 里包含 `npm run typecheck`、`npm run build -w @aihot/web`、`node --test apps/web/tests/*.test.ts`（CI 会装 chromium 和 webkit）以及 `npm test`（跑在 CI 的 PostgreSQL 上），另有迁移安全和站点 smoke 检查。也就是说本机缺的那部分由 CI 覆盖了。

## 兼容与使用影响

无。这个字段没有任何读取点，删除不改变运行时行为和配置语义；不涉及数据库、公开 API、`.env.example` 或升级步骤。已部署的站点若在自己仓库的 `site.ts` 里留了这个字段，删除后它只是不再出现，行为没有变化（它本就不生效）。

items.title: fix(github): keep the token out of the clone's remote URL
items.body:
Fixes #978.

## Problem

`ghRepoClone` — the clone path `teamai init` uses for the GitHub team repo — embeds the OAuth token in the clone URL:

```ts
const cloneUrl = token
  ? `https://x-access-token:${token}@github.com/${repo}.git`
  : `https://github.com/${repo}.git`;
```

Nothing resets it afterwards, so the token lives in `remote.origin.url`, i.e. in the clone's `.git/config`, where `git remote -v`, `git config --list`, a pasted log or an agent transcript all expose it.

## Why this shape

Both options in #978 are real, but taken literally either one leaves a hole:

- **Option 2 ("clone, then `git remote set-url`") alone regresses `push`.** Every push in `src/utils/git.ts` is a bare call (`:480`, `:512`, `:690`, `:694`), and `createGit` (`:88`) documents that auth "is handled by the provider's remote URL or by normal Git facilities". For the GitHub team repo the URL *is* the credential today — drop it and `push` has nothing to authenticate with.
- **Option 1 (header injection) exists only on the clone/fetch paths** (`clone.ts:163`, `gitlab-api.ts:187`). No push path takes an `http.extraHeader`, so applying it would mean threading credentials through every push call site.

So this PR uses each pattern where the repo already uses it:

1. **During the clone** — `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:<token>)>`, the same value `buildAuthHeader()` in `clone.ts:78` builds for its own GitHub path. The URL stays clean.
2. **After the clone** — persist a credential helper into the clone's local config, so the `push`/`pull` that `init` runs right after cloning still authenticate. This mirrors `cnbRepoClone` (`cnb-cli.ts:231`, `:246`, `:262`), which does exactly this and documents why: a `-c` option applies to that one invocation only.

The helper is `!"<absolute path to gh>" auth git-credential` when `gh` is installed — the absolute path, not a bare `gh`: `resolveCliPath` resolves `gh` through a login shell, while git runs `!` helpers through a non-login one, so a `gh` reachable only from a profile would be found at detection time and then not found at push time. This adds no new dependency — the provider already shells out to `gh` (`ghGetOAuthToken()` → `gh auth token`). And per gh's manual, `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` **take precedence over stored credentials**, so this covers the env-token case too. When `gh` is absent but a token is in the environment, it falls back to an inline helper that reads the same env vars at run time. Either way only the *command* is persisted — never the token.

## What changed

7 files, +341/-19.

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `src/providers/github/gh-cli.ts` | new `ghAuthHeader()` / `ghCredentialHelper()` / `ghCredentialHelperFor()` / `redactCredential()`; `ghRepoClone` clones with a clean URL + `-c http.extraHeader`, then persists a **URL-scoped** helper after clearing the inherited list, and redacts the injected credential out of a failed clone's message |
| `src/__tests__/github-provider.test.ts` | 12 new cases: header + clean URL + helper persisted; reset-then-add order; the env helper wins whenever an env token is set, even with `gh` installed; `ghCredentialHelperFor` decision rule; the persisted helper is the **absolute** gh path; no token → no helper; the url-embedded, trace2-argv and bare-token shapes are all redacted |
| `src/__tests__/provider-clone-windowshide.test.ts` | expected git launches for `ghRepoClone`: 1 → 3 (clone, `--replace-all`, `--add`) |
| `docs/providers.md` | clone row rewritten for the two-stage auth; new note on why the inherited helper list must be cleared first |
| `docs/designs/gitcode-provider.md` | the "GitHub embeds the token in the URL" precedent is gone — GitHub is no longer that shape |
| `src/providers/gitcode/gitcode-api.ts` | `cloneUrl` docstring: same stale "mirrors the GitHub (`x-access-token:<token>@`) provider" claim removed |
| `src/providers/cnb/cnb-cli.ts` | `cnbRepoClone` docstring: the "GitHub/TGit solve this by embedding the token in the clone URL" contrast loses GitHub — it is no longer in that group |

## Verification

### Real-CLI end-to-end

`teamai init` was run as a **built CLI** (`node <dist>/index.js init …`) against a local HTTPS smart-HTTP remote, with the clone URL left exactly as production builds it (`https://github.com/<org>/<repo>.git`) so the credential scope is real. Five arms, one variable at a time:

| arm | source | question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `PRE` | `main` | current behaviour |
| `HEAD` | the revision this PR previously pushed | what shipped before the review follow-up |
| `HEADRS` | `HEAD` + **only** the scope/reset fix | isolates the helper-ordering defect |
| `POST` | this revision | the behaviour being proposed |
| `NFF` | this revision minus the reset | negative control |

```
arm     exit clone content token_cfg scoped_reset fetch_pack push_advert push_pack
PRE     0    true  true    true      false        true       true        true
HEAD    0    true  true    false     false        true       false       false
HEADRS  0    true  true    false     true         true       false       false
POST    0    true  true    false     true         true       true        true
NFF     0    true  true    false     false        true       false       false
```

Reading it:

- **`PRE`** — `token_cfg=true`: the token is in the clone's `.git/config`. That is #978. Its push works only because the URL itself carries the credential.
- **`HEAD`** — nothing secret on disk, but the push fails. Its helper went in under the **unscoped** `credential.helper` key with a plain write, so it only appended to whatever the machine already had.
- **`HEADRS`** — adding *only* the scope + reset removes the `auth=other → 401` sequence from the server-side log; the inherited global helper stops answering. That single line is the whole of the ordering defect.
- **`POST`** — push is green end to end. The remote logged `GET /info/refs` → `401` → helper answers → `200`, then `POST /git-receive-pack` → `200`, with `Authorization: Basic x-access-token:`. `.git/config` holds the helper *command* and no secret.
- **`NFF`** — drop the reset and the inherited helper answers first (`auth=other → 401`); the CLI prints `⚠ Member registration could not be pushed (no write access?)`. This is the negative control that pins the reset as the cause rather than a correlation.

The two behaviours the review called out are therefore both reproduced and both fixed: the ordering problem only disappears when the key is scoped and cleared, and the token-precedence problem only disappears when the helper is chosen from the same source as the clone token.

### Credential redaction on the clone-failure path

`ghRepoClone` folds git's combined stdout/stderr into its `Error`. The guard it
applied only pattern-matched a token embedded in a **URL**; since the token now
travels in `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic <base64>`, that guard missed
it. Git prints its own argv at start-up when a trace2 sink is enabled, so the
argument came back on stderr and the base64 — reversible, i.e. the token in
disguise — landed in the message.

Reproduced and fixed with the same git, the same argv and the same environment
(`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT=1`); two arms, one variable:

| arm | call | credential in the output? |
|---|---|---|
| `R` | `git -c http.extraHeader=… clone …`, exactly what `ghRepoClone` spawns | **yes** — the trace2 `start` event prints `"argv":["git","-c","http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic eC1hY2Nlc3M…"]` |
| `F` | the built `ghRepoClone` | **no** — the same `argv` field now reads `"http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic ***"` |

Both arms fail locally (the destination is a non-empty directory, so git dies
before opening a transport): no network involved, and the `start` event is
written at process init regardless.

Measured, not assumed — which switches actually leak the blob:

| env | prints argv? | base64 reaches stderr? |
|---|---|---|
| `GIT_TRACE=1` | no | no |
| `GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1` / `GIT_TRACE_CURL=1` | — | no; git redacts the header it puts on the wire (`Authorization: Basic <redacted>`) |
| `GIT_TRACE2=1` / `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT=1` / `GIT_TRACE2_PERF=1` | yes | **yes** |

Redaction is by **value**, not by pattern: the exact `Authorization: Basic
<base64>` string that was injected, plus the raw token, are blanked wherever they
appear — the argv dump, the JSON `argv` array, and anything else git may choose
to print.

Negative control: with only the value-based redaction removed, **4 of the new
tests fail and 39 pass** — the tests detect the defect rather than merely
exercising the code.

### Static

- `vitest run` on the three affected test files → **65 passed** (43 + 5 + 17)
- `tsc --noEmit` → exits **0**
- `oxlint` `--deny-warnings` → **0 warnings / 0 errors** (814 files × 96 rules, repo-wide). The only warnings a full run reports come from `dist_e2e/`, an untracked local build output of the e2e harness above — not from source (`src/` alone: 808 files, still 0/0).

### Two probes worth keeping

- `git -c <header> clone` writes no auth blob; `git clone -c <header>` does, because `-c` after the subcommand is `--config`. The fix asserts that ordering.
- `git credential fill` against a clone produced by `POST` exits 0 and returns the secret from the environment, while `.git/config` stays token-free.

### Honest boundaries

- The harness is **local** — a CONNECT proxy plus TLS plus a hand-written smart-HTTP backend — not github.com. It drives the real CLI, real `git` and the real credential-helper protocol, but it cannot vouch for GitHub's server-side behaviour.
- `src/__tests__/e2e/e2e.test.ts:638` builds an `x-access-token:…@` URL itself via `execSync`; it does not go through `ghRepoClone` and is gated behind `CAN_RUN_REMOTE`, so it is left alone to keep the diff small. `docs/ci-e2e-setup.md` mirrors that same one-liner for manual repro — a setup instruction rather than a claim about what the provider does, so it is left as-is too.
- Rewriting the remote of **existing** clones (the `pull` / `doctor` part of #978) is still out of scope — it rewrites a URL a user's own `git push` may rely on. Happy to follow up separately.

items.title: fix(code-knowledge): veto a Swift bare call only inside a type body
items.body:
`#962` merged the Swift member-name veto, but the author's own follow-up commit landed on the branch **after** the squash, so `main` never got it. This PR carries that commit onto `main`, unchanged.

## This is a repair of a race, not a new idea

| | |
|---|---|
| `#962` merged | `2026-10-03T06:33:44Z` → squash `26016b11` |
| `#962` head when merged | `81bc89ba` |
| follow-up commit `ffd1de7` | *"veto a Swift bare call only inside a type body"*, authored `2026-10-03T06:35:30Z` — **1m46s after the merge** |
| `compare/main...ffd1de7` | `status=diverged`, `ahead_by=3` |

It was pushed to the PR branch, the bot reviewed it, and then the branch was already gone.

## Why it is not already in `main`

- `main`'s `call-resolver.ts` still reads an unconditional `!swiftModuleDeclaresMember(...)`
- the identifier `enclosedByType` appears **0** times anywhere in `main`'s ast sources
- `main`'s copy of the test file carries the first control (`still resolves a call no type in the module declares as a member`) but not the second

## What the fix changes, measured

A per-call-site question. Before, the member-name veto was put for **every** bare Swift call; now it is put only for a call a type lexically encloses.

Each row is a fixture run through `extractStructuralGraphAsFacts`, with the ast sources as the single variable (everything else in the tree held fixed):

| | call site | `main` (`26016b11`) | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | inherited member, call **inside** a type body | 0 | 0 |
| Q2 | inherited member, call in a **free function** | **0** | **1** |
| Q6 | inherited member, call in a func **nested inside** a free function | **0** | **1** |
| Q7 | inherited member, call at the **top level of a file** | **0** | **1** |
| Q8 | member is a **callable property**, call in a free function | **0** | **1** |
| Q5 | inherited member, call in a **closure inside** a type body | 0 | 0 |
| Q3 | control — no type declares the name, free function | 1 | 1 |
| Q4 | control — no type declares the name, inside a type body | 1 | 1 |

Four shapes get their edge back. Every one of them points at the module-level declaration, which is the only thing those calls could mean — the fix does not invent an edge, and the two shapes where a veto is genuinely right (Q1, Q5) still get it. The controls do not move.

## Failing test first

Same tree, `main`'s ast sources, only the test file swapped in:

```
FAIL  src/__tests__/ast-swift-module-scope.test.ts > Swift module-scope resolution (web-tree-sitter WASM)
      > still resolves a call no type encloses when an unrelated type declares the name
AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 43 passed (44)
```

Across the six suites that touch this layer:

| ast sources | result |
|---|---|
| `main` | `1 failed | 88 passed (89)` |
| this branch | `89 passed (89)` |

The single case that fails on `main` is the one this PR fixes. Nothing else moves in either direction.

## The change

| file | |
|---|---|
| `ast/walk.ts` | reports, per call site, whether a type lexically encloses it (`enclosedByType`, computed by the new `isInsideSwiftTypeBody`). `SWIFT_TYPE_BODIES` already exists on `main`. |
| `ast/types.ts` | the optional `enclosedByType` field on `AstCallSite` |
| `ast/call-resolver.ts` | asks the veto only where `site.enclosedByType === true` |
| `ast/module-scope.ts` | comment only — records that the caller decides which calls the question is put for |
| `__tests__/ast-swift-module-scope.test.ts` | the second control, alongside the existing one |

`+66/-5` across 5 files.

## What it does not do

Enclosure is **lexical**. A call inside a type body still loses its edge when an *unrelated* type declares a member of the same name (Q1 and Q5 stay at 0) — deciding whether the enclosing type is the one that declares the member needs the module's inheritance and conformance graph, which this layer does not build. That remains the accepted trade-off from `#962`, and the `module-scope.ts` comment says so. This change only stops the veto from reaching calls that no type encloses.

## Verification

- `vitest run` on the six ast suites (`ast-extract`, `ast-extract-swift`, `ast-import-resolver`, `ast-swift-module-scope`, `swift-extractor`, `namespace-resolver`): **89 passed / 0 failed**, against `1 failed | 88 passed` on `main` in the same setup
- `tsc --noEmit`: exit 0, no diagnostics
- `oxlint` on the five files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- each file byte-identical to upstream's blob at `ffd1de7` — `04f93fadad2d`, `fbf1724074e8`, `ef6c29ae070a`, `9cd8ac906cda`, `f741ceaea0cd`

### Real CLI, end to end (added after review)

The four bullets above cover unit, type and lint level only. The review asked for the same evidence at the level the change actually runs at, so this section is the end-to-end record: the bundled binary a user invokes, on real input, with the ast sources as the single variable.

### How the binary was produced

`npm run build` (tsup) cannot run on this machine — its `node_modules` is a shared tree missing `bundle-require`, so tsup exits 1 before bundling. The bundle was therefore produced with esbuild driven directly, using the settings `tsup.config.ts` declares: entry `src/index.ts`, `--format=esm`, `--target=node20`, out `dist/index.js`, shebang banner, sourcemap, dependencies external (tsup's default). Both arms go through the same bundler on the same tree — the only input that differs is the four ast files listed below. Each arm's `dist/index.js` is hashed and recorded.

### Command

Real process, no mocks:

```
node dist/index.js codebase --extract <fixture>
```

`codebase --extract` is the CLI surface that runs the AST track (`src/index.ts:1199` → `codebase-cmd.ts:43` → `codebase-extract.ts:651 extractStructuralGraphAsFacts`), which is the code this PR changes.

### Fixtures

Two tiny Swift modules. `veto` is the shape from this PR's own test; `ctrl` is the same module without the unrelated type.

```
veto/Sources/App/Global.swift    func work() -> Int { return 1 }
veto/Sources/App/Helper.swift    struct Helper { func work() -> Int { return 2 } }
veto/Sources/App/Runner.swift    func run() -> Int { return work() }

ctrl/Sources/App/Global.swift    func work() -> Int { return 1 }
ctrl/Sources/App/Runner.swift    func run() -> Int { return work() }
```

### Result

Three arms: the same tree, bundled three times with different ast sources. `PRE` is `main` before `#962` (no veto at all), `BASE` is `main` at `26016b11` (the squash of `#962` — the state this PR targets), `SHIP` is `ffd1de7`.

Cells are AST-derived relation facts for `Sources/App/Runner.swift → Sources/App/Global.swift`, cross-checked against `relation-*.md` and `.indices/graph-index.json`; all three projections agree in every cell.

| arm | ast source | `veto` | `ctrl` |
|---|---|---|---|
| PRE | `main` @ `83228692` (before `#962`) | 1 | 1 |
| BASE | `main` @ `26016b11` (`#962`) | **0** | 1 |
| SHIP | `ffd1de7` | **1** | 1 |

The CLI's own AST line, verbatim:

```
BASE/veto  [AST: ast: 4 symbols, 0 imports (0 resolved), 1 calls (0 resolved), 0 edges]
SHIP/veto  [AST: ast: 4 symbols, 0 imports (0 resolved), 1 calls (1 resolved), 1 edges]
```

`0 resolved / 0 edges` becomes `1 resolved / 1 edges`. Note this is the AST track **running and resolving nothing**, not the AST track being unavailable: that line only prints when `astAvailable()` is true, and the fallback path would have logged an `AST_UNAVAILABLE` gap instead.

The artifacts agree at the file level. `BASE/veto` produces **no `relation-*.md` at all** and reports `Facts: 4 (component:4)`. `SHIP/veto` produces `evidence/code/_cli966_fixture/relation-Sources.md` containing

```
- `Sources/App/Global.swift` ← Sources/App/Runner.swift:2
```

and reports `Facts: 5 (relation:1, component:4)`. All four runs exit 0.

### Single variable

The two ast trees differ in exactly four files — the four code files of `ffd1de7` — and in nothing else; the other seven are byte-identical. git blob shas (`main` @ `26016b11` → `ffd1de7`):

| file | BASE | SHIP |
|---|---|---|
| `ast/call-resolver.ts` | `c4a3e59fa4ee` | `04f93fadad2d` |
| `ast/module-scope.ts` | `f8ab2e4956c7` | `fbf1724074e8` |
| `ast/types.ts` | `01c14ef649ea` | `ef6c29ae070a` |
| `ast/walk.ts` | `b597b2d3b593` | `9cd8ac906cda` |

The `SHIP` column is byte-for-byte what this PR ships. sha1 of the bundled `dist/index.js`: BASE `ec5abd0f875e`, SHIP `9c051db5ff21`.

### Control

With no type declaring `work`, all three arms resolve the call. The fix does not disturb the case where nothing was vetoing it to begin with — it only stops the veto from reaching calls that no type encloses.

## Provenance

This is @Dev-next-gen's commit `ffd1de7`, carried over verbatim — cut onto `main` as-is, no edits. Credit for the fix is theirs; the only thing added here is getting it merged. Happy to close this if you would rather land it yourself, or if `#962` should simply be reopened.

items.title: fix(pull): do not self-heal the .gitignore under --dry-run
items.body:
## What

`pull` refreshes the team repo before it does anything else. In self mode that
refresh calls `migrateSelfModeGitignore`, which rewrites `.teamai/.gitignore` — a
**tracked** file in the member's own checkout — when it still has the pre-beta.5
shape (a bare `env` line that keeps team env vars off main).

`refreshTeamRepo(localConfig)` takes no options, so it cannot tell a preview from
a real run, and `pull` reaches it above every dry-run guard. `pull --dry-run`
therefore writes.

The refresh now takes `options` and runs the self-heal only when the run is real.
The migration is idempotent, so the next real pull performs it.

## Evidence

Real CLI, self-mode clone, `.teamai/.gitignore` = `token\nenv\nenv.local\n`,
committed to the checkout:

| | `.teamai/.gitignore` sha256 |
|---|---|
| before `pull --dry-run` | `ed747943d24dc463…` |
| after `pull --dry-run` | `f572d520732a16c2…` |

Whole-fixture tree hash: exactly one path differed — `app/.teamai/.gitignore` —
and nothing was removed. `pull` reported no error.

## Test

`dry-run-load-path.test.ts` already asserts, for a fresh self-mode clone, that
"nothing that already existed may be rewritten, whatever it is". Its fixture
(`setupSelfModeClone`) has no `.teamai/.gitignore` at all — and the migration
returns early when the file is missing — so the one path the refresh could write
to was the one path that fixture could not reach.

The new case adds the file to that same fixture and asserts the same thing:

| `pull.ts` (blob) | new case | whole file |
|---|---|---|
| main `509a8135` | fails — the file was rewritten | `1 failed / 94 passed` |
| this PR `7559d8d3` | passes | `95 passed / 0 failed` |

## Relation to #866

This is the one `[P1 blocking]` finding from the review on #866 that I could still
reproduce on `main` today. The lock-directory half was fixed in #896, and the
queued-learning publish is gated there as well. I have not re-measured the
remaining two.

The line is the one the review pointed at: `refreshTeamRepo` →
`migrateSelfModeGitignore` (now at `src/pull.ts:112`).

items.title: test(code-knowledge): make the assignment case pin the binding fix
items.body:
## What

`src/__tests__/ast-swift-module-scope.test.ts` — the case named "does not let an
assignment target stand in for a binding" used `alias = work()` as its fixture.
The name on the right of the assignment sits in a **call callee**, and the callee
form is skipped by both walkers. So the case produced the same 2 edges before and
after the fix it is supposed to guard, and passed on the base commit too.

This changes the fixture to the shape reported in the review on #928 —
`alias = work` followed by `work()` — and the expectation from 2 edges to 1.

That fix then drew a review comment here: the case now exercises the **value**
side of the assignment, while the name it carries describes the **target** side.
Both are real positions, so this revision covers both instead of renaming past
one of them:

- the case is renamed to `does not let an assignment value mention stand in for a
  binding`, which is what its fixture exercises;
- a second case takes the target-position name and a fixture that puts the
  referenced name where the name says it is — `alias = work` followed by
  `alias()`, with `func alias()` in a sibling file.

Two cases, because a regression can land on either side of the `=` independently,
and the value-position fixture cannot see the target side: its target is a name a
real `var` already bound.

## Evidence

The same test file, two walkers, one variable:

| `walk.ts` | fixture | edges | that assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| base `a504f8af` | `alias = work()` (before) | 2 | **passes** — which is the problem |
| base `a504f8af` | `alias = work` + `work()` | 0 | **fails** |
| main `f73493d4` | `alias = work` + `work()` | 1 | **passes** |

Whole file, after this revision: base `3 failed / 36 passed (39)`, main
`39 passed / 0 failed (39)`. The three base failures are the initializer case
#928 fixed, the value-position case, and the target-position case — the last two
are the ones this PR adds or repairs, and both are red on the walker the fix
replaced.

Which position is under test, same two-walker run:

| fixture | base `a504f8af` | main `f73493d4` |
|---|---|---|
| value position: `var alias = 0; alias = work; work()` | 0 | 1 |
| **target position: `alias = work; alias()`** | 0 | 1 |
| both sides cross-file: `alias = work; alias(); work()` | 0 | 2 |
| control: `work()` alone | 1 | 1 |
| control: `alias()` alone | 1 | 1 |
| control: `var alias = 0; alias = work; alias()` | 0 | 0 |

The last row is the reason the target-position case needs its own fixture: when
the target is a name a real `var` already bound, both walkers suppress the call,
so no fixture of that shape can distinguish them. The two rows above it are the
load-bearing ones — 0 against 1, on the same fixture, with only `walk.ts` swapped.

The first revision's `var alias = 0; alias = work` alone also reads 0 on both
walkers, which is why the case needs the call on the following line to be visible
at all.

## Why the counts fall where they do

An assignment binds its target, not the name on the right of the `=`. Reading
`work` there as if the assignment had declared it shadowed the module-level
`work`, so the call on the next line resolved to nothing — 0 edges. The fix reads
the grammar position instead, so only the call produces an edge.

The target-position case is the same rule read from the other side: neither side
of an assignment is a binding position, so `alias()` still answers to the sibling
file. A rule that read the target as a declaration would suppress it.

No source change; the walker on `main` already behaves correctly. This is a
test-only follow-up to #928.

items.title: fix(dry-run): thread { dryRun } through the loaders pull, push, status and list use
items.body:
## What this fixes

Fixes #850.

`--dry-run` is documented as *"Preview mode, no changes made"*, and #837 made that true for `tags subscribe`, `tags unsubscribe` and `roles set`. `pull`, `push` and `status` still wrote: the scope-detection block each runs **before any dry-run guard** called config loaders that were never given `{ dryRun }`.

The issue located the writes by code path and disclosed that the project-scope half — partition adoption and the self-heal bootstrap — had not been run. It is run below.

@ydflow's #853 landed the loader half (`loadLocalConfigForScope` gained `LoadOptions`) together with the `contribute` / `session save` / `recall` call sites. This PR is the remaining command-side half and nothing else.

## Change

The loaders already accept `LoadOptions`; these commands simply did not supply the flag.

| caller | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `pull.ts:1891` | `detectProjectConfig(undefined, sink)` | `…(undefined, sink, { dryRun: options.dryRun })` |
| `pull.ts:1924` | `loadLocalConfigForScope('user')` | `…('user', undefined, { dryRun: options.dryRun })` |
| `push.ts:731` | `autoDetectInit()` | `autoDetectInit(undefined, { dryRun: options.dryRun })` |
| `status.ts:52` | `autoDetectInit()` | `autoDetectInit(undefined, { dryRun: true })` |
| `status.ts:259` (`list`) | `autoDetectInit()` | `autoDetectInit(undefined, { dryRun: true })` |

`pull` and `push` carry their own `--dry-run`. `status` and `list` pass `{ dryRun: true }` unconditionally, as you asked in #850: they are read-only, so rather than reading the global flag they take the preview path every time — a read command should never migrate, adopt a partition or bootstrap. Callers that pass nothing behave as before, the same compatibility promise #837 made.

## Revision 2 — what the first head got wrong

The first head was red on `Lint & Test`, all four matrix entries. Two assertions in `src/__tests__/pull-scope-isolation.test.ts` were checking the exact argument list of the internal call this change widens:

```
expect(loadLocalConfigForScope).toHaveBeenCalledWith('user');
  received  ['user', undefined, { dryRun: undefined }]
```

Those two lines now name the third argument, and the source shape is not a free choice: `recall.ts:464` and `recall.ts:515` already call both loaders exactly this way — `(undefined, sink, { dryRun: options.dryRun })` and `('user', undefined, { dryRun: options.dryRun })` — landed with #853. So the call sites match the merged precedent rather than inventing a shape. `recall-scope-isolation.test.ts`, the parallel test of the parallel command, never asserts the argument list, which is exactly why the same change did not break it.

## Revision 3 — the two P1 findings

Both findings are correct, and they are one mistake in two places. The preview path returns a config that is *structurally identical* to a real one: `detectProjectConfig` / `autoDetectInit` under `{ dryRun }` hand back the config a bootstrap *would* have written, and nothing downstream can tell them apart. Revision 1 fixed which options the loaders get; it did not fix the two places that then **act** on what they loaded.

| finding | what the preview reached | what it left behind |
|---|---|---|
| `pull.ts:1891` → `lockScope()` (`pull.ts:1857`) | `acquireLock(<getDataHome>/.sync-lock)` → `ensureDir(path.dirname(...))` (`update.ts:392`) | the **partition directory** — absent on a fresh self-mode clone, and `releaseLock` deletes the lock file, not its parent |
| `push.ts:731` → the `kind === 'self'` branch (`push.ts:774`) | `acquireLock` → `migrateSelfModeGitignore()` → `withKnowledgeWorktree()`, all **before** `pushCore`'s own guard at `push.ts:1577` | the partition again, a rewritten `.teamai/.gitignore`, and a git worktree add/remove cycle |

### The fixture gap, which is the third time I picked a fixture wrongly

Correct finding, and worth naming properly: I chose the fixture from what I had rather than from the path the bug lives on. `dry-run-load-path.test.ts` *already had* a fresh-self-mode-clone fixture — but only `tags` and `roles` ran against it; `pull`/`push` ran at user scope, or on a project partition that already exists. A fresh clone is the one shape where `acquireLock` has something new to create.

Two cases added on that fixture. Same file, same fixture, single variable = the source under test:

```
                                  unfixed head    this revision
pull --dry-run  (fresh self-mode)   FAIL            PASS
push --dry-run  (fresh self-mode)   FAIL            PASS
                                    (the other 20 cases pass on both trees)
```

The unfixed failure is `expected true to be false` on `fs.existsSync(<HOME>/.teamai/projects)` — the reported symptom asserted by name, so it cannot pass for an unrelated reason. Nothing that already existed may be rewritten either, and the provider recorder must stay empty.

## Revision 4 — what Revision 3 got wrong, and CI saying so

Revision 3 shipped a guard at each call site: `lockScope()` returned `true` outright under a dry run, and the whole `kind === 'self'` branch returned early. That stopped every write, and it was still wrong.

`E2E (fork-safe, no credentials)` reported it. `src/__tests__/e2e/push-sync-followups-823.test.ts` failed 6 of 19, every failure the same shape:

```
AssertionError: expected '- Scanning local resources...\nℹ No n…'
  to contain '[rules] Skipped team-rule: .teamai/ru…'
Test Files  1 failed | 58 passed | 3 skipped (62)
```

A preview that reports *"No new or modified resources to push"* for a tree with a deliberately edited team rule is not a conservative preview — it is the same defect the PR exists to remove, with the sign flipped: it silently under-reports.

The cause is in `pushCore`'s own comment (`push.ts:1095-1112`), which describes what the worktree is for:

> the ACTIVE tree's `.teamai/{skills, rules}` … are diffed against the worktree checkout of `origin/<default>` (`localConfig.repo.localPath` here), so already-committed knowledge is skipped and only genuine additions/edits surface.

Outside the worktree, `projectRoot` and `repo.localPath` are the same directory in self mode, so that diff is empty by construction. **The worktree is not a side effect of pushing — it is the only source of the clean baseline the scanners compare against.** Skipping it does not report an edit early; it hides the edit.

### The fix, moved down to the primitive

The mistake was guarding at the call site. `lockScope()` returns a boolean its caller reads as *fact* — "do you hold the lock?" — so making it return `true` under a dry run **fabricated an assertion** rather than skipping a write. Same shape at `push.ts`, where the guard was wide enough to take the baseline with it.

So the guard is gone; the primitive answers instead. `acquireLock` gains an optional `options: { dryRun }` (`src/update.ts`), and under it asks the lock for its state instead of taking it:

```ts
if (options.dryRun) return (await lockState(resolved)) !== 'live';
```

- **It is exact.** `lockState` already separates `live` from `stale`/`missing`, and a real run reclaims either of the latter and wins — so the preview returns the answer the real command would have got. A scope or project with a live holder is now reported as contended, exactly as a real `pull`/`push` reports it, instead of being called uncontended.
- **It writes nothing.** No `ensureDir`, no lock file, no reclaim sentinel. `releaseLock` is safe to pair with it: it returns early when it holds no owner token for the path, so a preview cannot delete a lock another process owns.
- **What still skips, and why.** `migrateSelfModeGitignore()` rewrites a tracked file in the user's **active** tree, which outlives the preview; it is idempotent, so the next real push performs it. The git-mode clone refresh (`resetToCleanMaster` + `pullRepo`) keeps running, as in Revision 3 — that is what lets the preview name the destination the real command would use.
- The git-mode `sync-lock` at `push.ts:839` gets the same read-only treatment as the self-mode one.

The self-mode preview still needs the one read the worktree used to supply: the uncommitted `teamai.yaml` that `pushCore` receives as `initialPendingTeamConfig`. That block is `pendingSelfTeamConfig()` — the identical read, unchanged for the real path, called by the preview too.

The `<getDataHome>/locks/` entry in the fixture is unchanged and still declared, because the primitive was not the thing creating it — see the next section.

## One thing this revision does not fix, deliberately

`pull --dry-run` on a fresh self-mode clone still creates one **empty** directory: `<HOME>/.teamai/locks/`. Measured, not inferred — one probe, run unchanged against both trees:

```
pure main        pull --dry-run   added=[]                       (it never reaches the queue; 1 provider call)
this revision    pull --dry-run   added=["home\.teamai\locks/"]  (nothing else)
```

It comes from `listPendingForInstall` (`utils/pending-learnings.ts:183`), which `publishQueuedLearnings` calls to count the queue so `pull` can report how many learnings it would publish — and `withQueueLock` → `acquireLock` creates the lock's parent, on a call that passes no `dryRun`. It is pre-existing on the base commit as well; it became *reachable* on a fresh clone only now that detection stops aborting first.

I left it alone on purpose: that file is not part of this PR, and main rewrote it in #838 — the same commit that added the `dryRun` flag stopping just short of this call. Fixing it here means either shipping a copy of that file carrying #838's refactor, or editing the exact region #838 added; both turn this PR into a merge conflict with main. The test declares the entry and counts it (`expect({ appeared, vanished }).toEqual({ appeared: allowed, vanished: [] })`), so anything *else* appearing still fails the case. Worth a follow-up issue of its own — say the word and I will open one.

`push --dry-run` likewise leaves one `app/.git/FETCH_HEAD`: the preview now performs its `git fetch` for real, which is the point. It names no ref, changes no working tree, and git overwrites it on the next fetch. Same treatment — declared and counted.

## Verification

### Static checks

```
oxlint --deny-warnings --report-unused-disable-directives
  main + this change (merged tree)  rc=0  Found 0 warnings and 0 errors   (675 files)
  this branch tree                  rc=0  Found 0 warnings and 0 errors   (675 files)

tsc --noEmit
  main + this change  rc=0  0 diagnostics
  this branch tree    rc=0  0 diagnostics
```

The primitive was reviewed against its two callers before pushing, because both could have been silent breakage:

- `lockState` (`update.ts:246`) is read-only — one `readFile`, no branch that writes. The dry-run return is the first statement after `resolved` is computed, so no `ensureDir`, sentinel or `heldLockOwners` entry can be reached.
- `heldLockOwners.set` appears only on the three real-acquire paths, so under a dry run `releaseLock` finds no owner token and returns at its first line — it cannot delete a stale lock, or anyone else's.

### Command-level, single-variable control

`src/__tests__/dry-run-load-path.test.ts` already carried #837's fixture matrix and #853's loader cases. Seven cases are added, and every one of them **fails on unmodified `main` with the byte-identical test file** — the control tree is `main`'s `src` with this one test file dropped in, so the only variable is the source under test.

| case (fixture) | unmodified `main` | this change |
|---|---|---|
| `pull --dry-run` migrates nothing it loads (non-git, legacy role config) | FAIL | PASS |
| `push --dry-run` migrates nothing it loads | FAIL | PASS |
| `status` migrates nothing it loads | FAIL | PASS |
| `list` migrates nothing it loads | FAIL | PASS |
| `pull --dry-run` adopts no legacy partition on a git project | FAIL | PASS |
| `status` adopts no legacy partition on a git project | FAIL | PASS |
| `list` adopts no legacy partition on a git project | FAIL | PASS |

Each case snapshots every file under the fixture root (minus `debug.log` and git's transient locks, as the existing cases do) and asserts the tree is byte-identical afterwards, then asserts the provider recorder saw nothing and `updateReports` was not called.

```
dry-run-load-path.test.ts    unmodified main 13/22 pass   ->   this change 22/22 pass
                             9 cases discriminate (red on main, green here); 0 red on both trees

lock-atomic.test.ts                       pass  ->  pass   (acquireLock/releaseLock semantics)
pull-scope-isolation.test.ts             14/14 ->  14/14
```

### Real CLI, the issue's own reproduction

One isolated `HOME` holding a role-less `~/.teamai/config.yaml` next to a team repo whose `manifest/roles.yaml` declares `hai`; the CLI built from each tree; the only variable is the command.

| command | unmodified `main` | this change |
|---|---|---|
| `pull --dry-run` | **1 file written** — `~/.teamai/config.yaml` gains `scope: user`, `additionalRoles: []`, `primaryRole: hai`, `resourceProfileVersion: 1` | **0 files written** |
| `status` | the same 1 file | **0 files written** |
| `list` | the same 1 file | **0 files written** |

6/6, re-run after Revision 3 against the merge result (`main@5fb316c7` + this change) rather than the earlier snapshot, since a stale e2e is what the guards were added to fix.

### What I could not adjudicate locally, and what I did instead

This machine blocks **synchronous** child processes (`spawnSync` / `execFileSync` answer `EBUSY`, including with the sandbox disabled — an antivirus/system layer, not our code). `push-sync-followups-823.test.ts` sets up its fixtures through `execFileSync('git', …)`, so every one of its 19 cases dies in `beforeEach` with `Hook timed out in 15000ms` here — exactly the 6 failures this revision is about, from the opposite direction: locally they never even get to assert.

That is why the E2E verdict is CI's to give, and why the local evidence above is scoped to what does run: `tsc`, `oxlint`, and the non-E2E set. Of the 27 non-E2E test files that touch `acquireLock` / `releaseLock`, the ones that do not also shell out synchronously to git pass. The rest were run on both trees — unmodified base and this revision — and **every failure on both is a timeout (`Hook timed out in 15000ms` / `Test timed out in 15000ms`), with zero assertion failures on either**. The file count that differs between those two runs (5 vs 6 red) is therefore machine scheduling under a hung `git`, not this change; and it is the same reason I cannot produce a local verdict on `push-sync-followups-823.test.ts`, which is the file that actually discriminates.

## Scope

- **In:** the four call sites, the read-only acquisition the two acting sites now use, and the test matrix.
- **Out:** `init`'s call sites (it has no `--dry-run` to honour), the git-mode clone refresh a preview performs on purpose, and the `<HOME>/.teamai/locks/` directory described above — upstream `listPendingForInstall`, tracked separately rather than patched from here.
- **Still unaudited, and deliberately so:** `requireInitForScope` (`config.ts:625`) takes no `options` and calls `loadLocalConfigForScope` bare. It has no caller anywhere in `src/`, so it reads as exported surface rather than a live path; I left it alone rather than guess at its contract. Worth a follow-up if you want it threaded or removed.

items.title: fix(code-knowledge): collect Swift shadowing from binding positions
items.body:
**Follow-up to #847** (merged as `2aaf3db`). Not a complaint about the merge —
the resolution change itself is what I wanted. This carries the one finding of
that PR's last re-review that rode in with it. I asked on #847 whether it had been
noticed ([comment](https://github.com/Tencent/teamai-cli/pull/847#issuecomment-5905478326))
and said I would open a fresh PR if there was no reply, so the fix arrives here
rather than as another push to a branch that is dead after the squash.

Authored on `main` at `128844fe6c4b`. The three files it touches are byte-identical
on that base to `8b4e67c0` (`walk.ts` blob `a504f8af`, `types.ts` `8feaa29c`, the
test `63be4dac`), so everything measured below describes the code this lands on.

## What is wrong on `main` today

`src/wiki-engine/code-knowledge/ast/walk.ts` collects the names that shadow a
bare call, and it asked whether a name *occurs* anywhere in the declaring
declaration — other than in the one argument position the previous round carved
out. Every remaining expression position satisfies that, so a mention was counted
as a binding:

```swift
func run() {
  let alias = work   // this `work` is a use
  work()             // ...and it suppressed the edge for this call
}
```

Same defect, same cause, wherever an identifier that is *not* the thing being
bound sits inside the declaration — `let f = work`, `a = work`, the sequence `xs`
in `for work in xs`, the subject `x` in `switch x { case let work: }`. The
re-review named the initializer; the assignment form is the same bug one position
over. (The previous round carved out the argument position, `consume(work)`, which
is why that one no longer does this — and why it was clear the carve-out would not
be the last.) Subtracting one position per review does not converge, so this
changes the question instead: a name now counts when the identifier is where a
name is **bound**, read off its parent node (a grammar `name` / `bound_identifier`
field, or a `pattern` / `type_parameter` container). That set is fixed by the
language, not by the review. What the file loses: the `insideArgument` marker, the
`call_expression` callee-skip and the marker's propagation through
`value_arguments` / `lambda_literal`. The `pattern` / `type_parameter` check is not
a special case any more either — it *is* the rule, inside `isSwiftBindingPosition`.
The added lines are the comments that state it (net `+75/-57` on the file).

On the released `main`, verified by pulling the file and running the shapes:

| shape | `main` | expect | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `func run() { let alias = work; work() }` | **0 edges** | 1 | 1 |
| `func run() { let f = work; work() }` | **0** | 1 | 1 |
| `func run() { var a = 0; a = work; work() }` | **0** | 1 | 1 |
| `func run() { let work = 1; work() }` — a real binding | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `func run() { let alias = makeWork(); work() }` | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| `func run() { work() }` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

## Real CLI verification

The package was built and its own command run, base against change, over a
two-file fixture — output read from the files it wrote, not from a harness:

```
Sources/App/Worker.swift   func work() -> Int { return 1 }
Sources/App/B.swift        func run() { let alias = work; work() }

$ teamai codebase --extract <fixture> --json
```

| walk.ts | CLI report | REFERENCES edges |
|---|---|---|
| base (`main`) | 2 files, 2 facts, 4 nodes / 1 edge | **0** |
| this PR | 2 files, 3 facts, 5 nodes / 3 edges | **1** — `Sources/App/B.swift -> Sources/App/Worker.swift` |

and the extractor's own relation document
`teamwiki/evidence/code/<project>/relation-Sources.md` carries it as

```
- `Sources/App/Worker.swift` ← `Sources/App/B.swift:3`
```

which is the call in question. That document is the whole of the delta under
`teamwiki/`: byte-comparing the two trees, exactly one file is added (it) and
eight are edited because they embed it — the graph index, the facts and interface
caches, the code-project manifest, its index and overview pages, the root index,
and the source manifest. Nothing is removed. In `graph-index.json` the node set is
identical and the edge set goes 1 → 3: the REFERENCES edge above, plus a CONTAINS
edge for the new document.

## Evidence

- **19-shape matrix**: **0 regressions, 1 repair**, controls untouched. The
  comparison is the `8b4e67c0` content (what `main` carries for these files)
  against this commit — not two states of my own branch.
- **27 shapes**, binding sets old rule vs new: they differ on **8 rows**, and every
  difference *removes* a name — no row gains one, and no row loses a name the body
  can bind. The eight: the initializer's and the assignment's mention of `work`
  itself; the optional `opt` in `if let` and in `guard let`; the array `xs` in
  `for work in xs`; the subject `x` of a `switch` with `case let work`; the value
  `y` in a type annotation; and the external argument label of
  `func run(label work:)`, which the body cannot see at all.
- **Tests**: `ast-swift-module-scope.test.ts` 36 → 38, all pass; the four AST
  suites 70 passed.
- **Mutations**: 5 mutants, 4 killed. See the survivor below.
- **Cost**: one traversal per declaration; at 1600 calls the two versions are
  within a few percent either way (37.2 / 36.2 / 37.8 ms against 35.0 / 39.8 /
  41.2 ms), and the time grows 3.8–4.0x for an 8x call count.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `oxlint --deny-warnings` rc=0 locally; the `--type-aware`
  half runs in CI.

## Two things worth flagging rather than burying

1. **My previous matrix had this defect scored as correct.** The row occupied by
   `let f = work; work()` was scored `expect none` — the *measured* value written
   down as the required one. The matrix did not miss the defect; it certified it.
   Corrected here, with a companion row for the assignment form.
2. **One of five mutants survives** — removing the `user_type` guard. It is an
   equivalent mutant under this grammar, not an unreached branch: with the guard
   removed the binding sets over ten type positions are identical. The guard is
   kept as the explicit statement of the constraint.

## Scope

- `#909` (inherited and cross-file extension members) is untouched and remains
  the one blocking finding. It needs a member table the AST index does not build,
  so no amount of position handling reaches it.
- The branch `fix/843-swift-module-scope` is dead after the squash merge; this
  arrives on a fresh branch off `main`.

items.title: Backend: the Markdown export filename follows the site's own identity, not AIHOT
items.body:
fork 出来改成自己行业的站，后端还有一处把 AIHOT 的名字写进了读者下载到的文件里。这个 PR 把它改成读站点自己的配置。
